1	/* The control socket's reply lines (D-043, D-045): what statusd reads from a source.
2	 *
3	 * A reply is zero or more record lines, then one terminator, each line ending in "\n"
4	 * (a "\r\n" is accepted):
5	 *
6	 *     proc name="obdd" up=1 pid=412 src="synth"  a record: a tag, then key=value fields
7	 *     ok                                         the end of a good reply
8	 *     err unavailable storaged is down           the end of a refused one: a code, then text
9	 *
10	 * Tags, keys and codes are [a-z0-9_]. A value carries its type: in double quotes it is a
11	 * string (printable ASCII, no '"' and no '\', so nothing is unescaped), bare it is a JSON
12	 * number (json.h) or null, and anything else bare is refused. So pid="46" and pid=46 are
13	 * different things, and forgetting the quotes is an error, not a silent change of type.
14	 * Parsing copies into fixed-size fields: no allocation, and the caller's buffer can go
15	 * away afterward.
16	 */
17	#ifndef CARWATCH_KV_H
18	#define CARWATCH_KV_H
19	
20	#include <stddef.h>
21	
22	#define KV_MAX_LINE     512u   /* bytes in a line, not counting its newline */
23	#define KV_MAX_FIELDS   16u
24	#define KV_MAX_TAG      24u    /* these sizes count the NUL */
25	#define KV_MAX_KEY      24u
26	#define KV_MAX_VALUE    96u
27	#define KV_MAX_CODE     24u
28	#define KV_MAX_REASON   96u
29	
30	typedef enum {
31	    KV_RECORD,       /* a tag and its fields */
32	    KV_OK,           /* the end of a good reply */
33	    KV_ERR,          /* the end of a refused reply: err_code and err_reason are set */
34	    KV_BAD,          /* malformed, or over a limit */
35	    KV_INCOMPLETE    /* no whole line yet, or no terminator yet */
36	} kv_kind_t;
37	
38	typedef enum { KV_STR, KV_NUM, KV_NULL } kv_type_t;
39	
40	typedef struct {
41	    char      key[KV_MAX_KEY];
42	    char      val[KV_MAX_VALUE];   /* a string without its quotes; a number or "null" as typed */
43	    kv_type_t type;
44	} kv_field_t;
45	
46	typedef struct {
47	    char       tag[KV_MAX_TAG];
48	    kv_field_t f[KV_MAX_FIELDS];
49	    size_t     nfields;
50	    char       err_code[KV_MAX_CODE];
51	    char       err_reason[KV_MAX_REASON];   /* "" if the line gave none */
52	} kv_line_t;
53	
54	/* Parses one line, s[0, len), without its newline. s need not be NUL-terminated. *out is
55	 * cleared first and is meaningful only for KV_RECORD and KV_ERR. */
56	kv_kind_t kv_parse_line(const char *s, size_t len, kv_line_t *out);
57	
58	/* Takes the next line from [*cursor, end) and parses it. Advances *cursor past the line's
59	 * newline, even when the line is KV_BAD, so a caller can skip it. Returns KV_INCOMPLETE,
60	 * leaving *cursor alone, if no newline remains. */
61	kv_kind_t kv_reply_next(const char **cursor, const char *end, kv_line_t *out);
62	
63	/* Walks a whole reply, buf[0, len), and says how it ended: KV_OK, or KV_ERR with *final
64	 * set (final may be NULL). KV_BAD if any line is bad or anything follows the terminator;
65	 * KV_INCOMPLETE if the reply stops before its terminator and that terminator's newline. */
66	kv_kind_t kv_reply_check(const char *buf, size_t len, kv_line_t *final);
67	
68	/* The value of key on a record line, or NULL if it has none. */
69	const char *kv_get(const kv_line_t *line, const char *key);
70	
71	#endif

/* statusd's routes (D-043, D-045): the handler that server.c calls for each request. It
 * maps a URL to one request line for the source, and turns the source's reply into JSON.
 * No sockets and no allocation; the 64 KB scratch buffer is the caller's.
 *
 *   /                      a placeholder page (see route.c: it is replaced by the real page)
 *   /api/status            status
 *   /api/verdicts          verdicts
 *   /api/faults            faults
 *   /api/series?pid=&from=&to=
 *                          series pid="..." from=... to=...
 *
 * Success is 200 with {"ok":true,"records":[{"tag":"proc","name":"obdd","pid":102,...}]},
 * each field typed as the source typed it (kv.h). Every refusal under /api/ is JSON too,
 * {"ok":false,"code":"usage","reason":"..."}, so the page can always parse a body.
 *
 * Whatever the URL carries is untrusted, and a request line is built from it. So query
 * keys are checked against a fixed list, each value must be 1 to 24 bytes of
 * [A-Za-z0-9:+.,_/-] after decoding, and anything else is a 400 that never reaches the
 * source. The routes take no other query: an unexpected key, a repeated one, or any query
 * on a route that takes none is a 400. A "+" in a URL decodes to a space, so a client that
 * means a plus sends %2B.
 */
#ifndef CARWATCH_ROUTE_H
#define CARWATCH_ROUTE_H

#include "interface/http.h"
#include "interface/server.h"
#include "interface/source.h"

#define ROUTE_REPLY_MAX  65536u

typedef struct {
    const source_t *src;
    char            reply[ROUTE_REPLY_MAX];   /* the source's text, before it becomes JSON */
} route_ctx_t;

/* A server_handler_t: ctx is a route_ctx_t whose src is set. */
void route_handle(void *ctx, const http_request_t *req, server_response_t *resp);

#endif

1	/* statusd's HTTP layer (D-043): bytes in, bytes out, no sockets.
2	 *
3	 * Only GET is served. HEAD is refused on purpose (405, with "Allow: GET"): nothing we
4	 * serve is asked for with it. The parser takes whatever has been read so far and says
5	 * whether it is a whole request, part of one, or one to refuse; the writer makes the head
6	 * of a response and leaves the body to the caller, so the embedded page is never copied.
7	 * Every buffer is fixed-size: a request cannot make this layer allocate.
8	 */
9	#ifndef CARWATCH_HTTP_H
10	#define CARWATCH_HTTP_H
11	
12	#include <stddef.h>
13	#include <sys/types.h>
14	
15	#define HTTP_MAX_REQUEST   4096u   /* request line and headers together */
16	#define HTTP_PATH_MAX      128u
17	#define HTTP_QUERY_MAX     256u
18	
19	/* The statuses this layer can write. http_write_head refuses any other. */
20	typedef enum {
21	    HTTP_STATUS_OK                  = 200,
22	    HTTP_STATUS_BAD_REQUEST         = 400,
23	    HTTP_STATUS_NOT_FOUND           = 404,
24	    HTTP_STATUS_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED  = 405,
25	    HTTP_STATUS_HEADERS_TOO_LARGE   = 431,
26	    HTTP_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR      = 500,
27	    HTTP_STATUS_UNAVAILABLE         = 503   /* a process behind us is down or not ready */
28	} http_status_t;
29	
30	/* A refusal is its own HTTP status, so a caller answers with the value it was given. The
31	 * two non-refusals are outside the status range: HTTP_OK does not say which status the
32	 * route will answer with, and HTTP_INCOMPLETE is not an answer yet. */
33	typedef enum {
34	    HTTP_INCOMPLETE = -1,   /* read more and call again */
35	    HTTP_OK = 0,            /* a whole, acceptable request */
36	    HTTP_BAD = HTTP_STATUS_BAD_REQUEST,                /* malformed, or a target we refuse */
37	    HTTP_BAD_METHOD = HTTP_STATUS_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED,  /* anything but GET */
38	    HTTP_TOO_LARGE = HTTP_STATUS_HEADERS_TOO_LARGE     /* no end of headers in the cap */
39	} http_parse_t;
40	
41	typedef struct {
42	    char path[HTTP_PATH_MAX];     /* starts with '/', still percent-encoded */
43	    char query[HTTP_QUERY_MAX];   /* after the '?', still percent-encoded; "" if none */
44	} http_request_t;
45	
46	/* Parses buf[0, len), which need not be NUL-terminated. Fills *out only on HTTP_OK.
47	 * Headers are checked for stray control bytes and then ignored. */
48	http_parse_t http_parse_request(const char *buf, size_t len, http_request_t *out);
49	
50	/* Finds key in an "a=1&b=2" query, percent-decodes its value into out[n] ('+' is a
51	 * space), and returns 0. Returns -1 if the key is absent, the encoding is bad, or the
52	 * value does not fit. */
53	int http_query_get(const char *query, const char *key, char *out, size_t n);
54	
55	/* Writes the status line and headers, ending with the blank line, for a response whose
56	 * body is body_len bytes of ctype. The head is NUL-terminated, so cap must be its length
57	 * plus one. Returns the length written (not counting the NUL), or -1 if cap is too small
58	 * or status is not an http_status_t this layer knows. */
59	ssize_t http_write_head(char *out, size_t cap, int status, const char *ctype,
60	                        size_t body_len);
61	
62	#endif
63

### B.6 — The phone page also downloads a report; an app is a stretch ⚠️ UNREVIEWED

`D-028` · Decided M2, 2026-10-21 · **By:** Camden (in session) + Claude
· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
· **Extends:** D-013 (§B.4)

**Decision.** The status page (D-013) shows status, current verdicts and trends, and has
one button: **Download report**. The report is one self-contained HTML file plus a CSV of
the same data, generated on the box by a C program in `src/interface/`. The page still
writes nothing to the device. A native phone app is a stretch goal, not planned for M2 to
M5.

**Report contents** (first draft; finalized in `reportspec`):

| Section | Content |
| --- | --- |
| Header | Box id, report time, whether wall-clock time is trustworthy, and the mix of data sources (`live`, `replay`, `synth`), always labeled (C.2) |
| Sessions | Each key cycle: boot id, start, end, duration, ended cleanly or recovered, records lost on recovery |
| Box health | Process liveness and restarts, ring overruns (must be zero), undervoltage and throttle events, temperature, the supercapacitor's self-check, free storage |
| Car findings | Each surfaced verdict: fault area, the sensors that cooperated to call it, residual and trend evidence, when it began and ended, confidence |
| Baseline maturity | Hours of normal driving learned per operating-point bin, so the owner knows how far to trust the verdicts |

6	 *   /api/status            status
7	 *   /api/verdicts          verdicts
8	 *   /api/faults            faults
9	 *   /api/series?pid=&from=&to=
10	 *                          series pid="..." from=... to=...

12	 * Success is 200 with {"ok":true,"records":[{"tag":"proc","name":"obdd","pid":102,...}]},
13	 * each field typed as the source typed it (kv.h). Every refusal under /api/ is JSON too,

16	 * Whatever the URL carries is untrusted, and a request line is built from it. So query
17	 * keys are checked against a fixed list, each value must be 1 to 24 bytes of
18	 * [A-Za-z0-9:+.,_/-] after decoding, and anything else is a 400 that never reaches the
19	 * source. The routes take no other query: an unexpected key, a repeated one, or any query
20	 * on a route that takes none is a 400. A "+" in a URL decodes to a space, so a client that
21	 * means a plus sends %2B.
22	 */

1	/* statusd's HTTP layer (D-043): bytes in, bytes out, no sockets.
2	 *
3	 * Only GET is served. HEAD is refused on purpose (405, with "Allow: GET"): nothing we
4	 * serve is asked for with it. The parser takes whatever has been read so far and says
5	 * whether it is a whole request, part of one, or one to refuse; the writer makes the head
6	 * of a response and leaves the body to the caller, so the embedded page is never copied.
7	 * Every buffer is fixed-size: a request cannot make this layer allocate.
8	 */
9	#ifndef CARWATCH_HTTP_H
10	#define CARWATCH_HTTP_H
11	
12	#include <stddef.h>
13	#include <sys/types.h>
14	
15	#define HTTP_MAX_REQUEST   4096u   /* request line and headers together */
16	#define HTTP_PATH_MAX      128u
17	#define HTTP_QUERY_MAX     256u
18	
19	/* The statuses this layer can write. http_write_head refuses any other. */
20	typedef enum {
21	    HTTP_STATUS_OK                  = 200,
22	    HTTP_STATUS_BAD_REQUEST         = 400,
23	    HTTP_STATUS_NOT_FOUND           = 404,
24	    HTTP_STATUS_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED  = 405,
25	    HTTP_STATUS_HEADERS_TOO_LARGE   = 431,
26	    HTTP_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR      = 500,
27	    HTTP_STATUS_UNAVAILABLE         = 503   /* a process behind us is down or not ready */
28	} http_status_t;
29	
30	/* A refusal is its own HTTP status, so a caller answers with the value it was given. The
31	 * two non-refusals are outside the status range: HTTP_OK does not say which status the
32	 * route will answer with, and HTTP_INCOMPLETE is not an answer yet. */
33	typedef enum {
34	    HTTP_INCOMPLETE = -1,   /* read more and call again */
35	    HTTP_OK = 0,            /* a whole, acceptable request */
36	    HTTP_BAD = HTTP_STATUS_BAD_REQUEST,                /* malformed, or a target we refuse */
37	    HTTP_BAD_METHOD = HTTP_STATUS_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED,  /* anything but GET */
38	    HTTP_TOO_LARGE = HTTP_STATUS_HEADERS_TOO_LARGE     /* no end of headers in the cap */
39	} http_parse_t;
40	
41	typedef struct {
42	    char path[HTTP_PATH_MAX];     /* starts with '/', still percent-encoded */
43	    char query[HTTP_QUERY_MAX];   /* after the '?', still percent-encoded; "" if none */
44	} http_request_t;
45	
46	/* Parses buf[0, len), which need not be NUL-terminated. Fills *out only on HTTP_OK.
47	 * Headers are checked for stray control bytes and then ignored. */
48	http_parse_t http_parse_request(const char *buf, size_t len, http_request_t *out);
49	
50	/* Finds key in an "a=1&b=2" query, percent-decodes its value into out[n] ('+' is a
51	 * space), and returns 0. Returns -1 if the key is absent, the encoding is bad, or the
52	 * value does not fit. */
53	int http_query_get(const char *query, const char *key, char *out, size_t n);
54	
55	/* Writes the status line and headers, ending with the blank line, for a response whose
56	 * body is body_len bytes of ctype. The head is NUL-terminated, so cap must be its length
57	 * plus one. Returns the length written (not counting the NUL), or -1 if cap is too small
58	 * or status is not an http_status_t this layer knows. */
59	ssize_t http_write_head(char *out, size_t cap, int status, const char *ctype,
60	                        size_t body_len);
61	
62	#endif

Written for you, Lance. This is the step 6 breakdown, based on the code step 5 landed. I haven't edited anything.

## What step 5 left us

- **Response buffer:** `route_handle` ([route.c:205](src/interface/route.c#L205)) fills a `server_response_t`. Its body buffer is 48 KB (`SERVER_BODY_MAX`).
- **Source reply buffer:** the source's text goes into a separate 64 KB `rc->reply`.
- **`series` is per PID:** a CSV of all signals needs one `source_query` per PID.
- **What the synth source returns:** `sample` rows, plus `verdict` rows carrying `area`, `sensors`, `residual`, `state`, `start_s` and `end_s`. `end_s` can be `null`, and every row carries `src="synth"`.
- **No PID list exists:** no verb lists the PIDs, so `/report.csv` has to know which ones to ask for.

## Proposed split: three commits instead of one

The plan has one commit. I'd split it the way step 3 split `json.c` off from the converter. Each commit is then one yes/no for the reviewer.

1. `M3 interface: write CSV with quoting`: `csv.c`, `csv.h`, `test_csv.c`. A pure unit with no sockets.
2. `M3 interface: share the source round-trip in route.c`: a no-behavior-change refactor. CLAUDE.md §7.3 wants refactors labeled and separate.
3. `M3 interface: add the CSV report route`: `report.c`, `report.h`, the hook in `route_handle`, tests, and the D-045 text fix.

## Commit 1: `csv.h` / `csv.c`

The API mirrors `json.h`: caller-owned buffer, sticky errors, one check at the end.

| Method | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `csv_init(csv_t*, char *buf, size_t cap, unsigned ncols)` | Sets the buffer and the column count. |
| `csv_text(csv_t*, const char *s)` | Writes a text field. It quotes the field if it holds `,` `"` CR or LF, and doubles any inner quote. A field starting with `= + - @` or tab gets a leading `'`, which stops Excel reading it as a formula. A byte of 0x80 or more, or a control byte other than CR or LF inside a quoted field, fails the writer. |
| `csv_number(csv_t*, const char *text)` | Writes raw only if `json_is_number` accepts it, otherwise fails. This is where `-3.2` stays a number and isn't mangled by the formula guard. |
| `csv_empty(csv_t*)` | An empty field, used for `null`. |
| `csv_end_row(csv_t*)` | Writes `\r\n` (RFC 4180). Fails if the row doesn't have exactly `ncols` fields, so the file can't be ragged. |
| `csv_finish(csv_t*)` | Returns the length, or -1 if the writer failed. It also fails on a half-written row. |

Tests to write first and see fail:
- a plain row;
- comma, quote and newline quoting;
- the `=1+1` guard against `-3.2` unguarded;
- `null` becoming an empty field;
- a short and a long row both failing;
- non-ASCII failing;
- a one-byte-short buffer returning -1 and never writing past the end.

## Commit 2: refactor in `route.c`

Pull the block at [route.c:240-262](src/interface/route.c#L240-L262) into one helper:

- `static source_result_t ask_source(route_ctx_t*, const char *line, size_t *n, kv_line_t *final)`. It runs `source_query` and `kv_reply_check`, and returns OK, ERR (with `final` set), TOO_BIG or MALFORMED.
- `route_handle` keeps its JSON path and calls the helper.
- The existing `test_route.c` is the proof that nothing changed.

The report needs the same checks, so the alternative is copying them. A shared helper is the smaller long-term diff.

## Commit 3: `report.c`

| Method | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `void report_handle(route_ctx_t*, const http_request_t*, server_response_t*)` | Entry point, called from `route_handle` when the path is `/report.csv`. Any query gives 400, as on the other routes. It writes the header, then one `series` per PID, then `verdicts`. The first failure aborts the whole report, with the source's error mapped through the existing `status_for_code`. It never sends a partial CSV, so a file can't look complete when it isn't. |
| `static bool emit_header(csv_t*)` | Writes `kind,t_s,name,value,detail,src`. |
| `static bool append_reply(csv_t*, const char *reply, size_t n, row_fn)` | Walks the reply with `kv_reply_next`. For each record it requires `src` to be present and a string, then calls the row function. A record with no `src` fails the report, because §2.7 says never to invent one. |
| `static bool sample_row(csv_t*, const kv_line_t*)` | `sample,<t_s>,<pid>,<value or empty>,,<src>`. |
| `static bool verdict_row(csv_t*, const kv_line_t*)` | `verdict,<start_s>,<area>,<residual>,"sensors=…;state=…;end_s=…",<src>`. |

- **Rows keep the source's `src` value** rather than hardcoding `synth`. That keeps the real source honest later.
- **Response:** content type `text/csv; charset=utf-8`.
- **Buffers:** each PID's reply goes through `rc->reply` and is converted straight into `resp->body`. Nothing is held between PIDs.

Tests in `test_route.c`, using a stub source:
- 200 with the exact header;
- every data row ends in `,synth`;
- row count equals 7 PIDs × samples plus the verdicts;
- a comma inside `detail` comes out quoted;
- a stub `err unavailable` gives 503 with no partial body;
- a record missing `src` gives 500;
- a query gives 400.

In `test_statusd.c`, one live `/report.csv` fetch checks that every line ends in `synth`.

The same commit edits the "What is already coded" paragraph in D-045, which currently says the CSV is still to come. It also updates the route list in `route.h`. It doesn't tick `report`, which is a human act and covers the HTML report too.

## Decisions I need from you

1. **PID list.** Nothing in the source says which PIDs exist. I recommend hardcoding the seven synth PIDs in `report.c` as `report_pids[]`, with an open `milestones.md` box for a source-side listing when `ctlsource` lands. The alternative is a new `pids` verb, which changes D-043 and needs its own decision. Is the hardcoded list OK?
2. **Size ceiling.** At the default 5-minute window there are about 150 samples per PID. Seven PIDs come to about 40 KB of CSV, which is close to the 48 KB cap. A real car publishes more PIDs, so it will overflow. On overflow I'd return a 500 and not truncate, because truncating is dishonest. Raising `SERVER_BODY_MAX` or streaming the body is its own later change. I'd put it on the board and not fix it here. Agreed?
3. **Download header.** `Content-Disposition: attachment` would need a change in `http.c`. I'd skip it and have step 7's page link use `<a download>`.
4. **Schema.** I chose one flat table (`kind,t_s,name,value,detail,src`) over several sections. That's easier for a mechanic's spreadsheet, and the unit tests are simpler. The cost is that `detail` is a packed string for verdicts.

If you agree, I'll update the plan file with this and renumber the later steps. I can start the branch work after that.

# Plan: `statusd`, the on-box status website (dummy data first, logs served as they are)

## Context

D-013/D-028/D-043 already name this process: `statusd`, C, in `src/interface/`, the only
`AF_INET` process, serving the phone page over the box's own Wi-Fi. Board item `statusd`
(#177, "runs as a supervised child and is built by the Makefile") is the open box;
`phoneview` (M4) and `report` (M3) are the later content items. The goal now: a working site
showing faults/verdicts, process health, trends and a **log download**, with the live
panels fed by **synthetic** values behind a seam, so the real OBD2/analysis data plugs in
later with no page changes.

Decisions already made with the user: server in **C** (matches D-043); **standalone
binary now**, supervisor spawning stays with `supfork` (#41); page scope = faults list,
process health, trends + log download. A small "latest values" strip is included because
trends are meaningless without current readings (flag in review if unwanted).

**Changed 2026-10-28 (user): no generated CSV.** The device already keeps the data:
`storaged` writes `log-<first seq>.cwr` segments (D-034: 16 MB, CRC'd, append-only,
every record carries `src`). Building a CSV from the source would store the same data a
second time, in a second format, with a second labeling path. So `statusd` serves those
segment files byte for byte, and a tool off the box turns them into CSV. `statusd` never
parses a record.

## Design

**The seam (live panels).** D-043 says the page is built from control-socket verbs
(`status`, `verdicts`, `series`, `faults`; reply = `key=value` lines then `ok`). So
`statusd` talks to a *source* with one function: `source_query(verb, args, out_buf)`
returning exactly that D-043 text. Two implementations behind one header:
- `synth_source.c` (done): deterministic fake data, every record `src=synth`.
- `ctl_source.c` (later, not in this PR): connects to `/run/carwatch/ctl.sock`.
Swapping = one line in `statusd_main.c`. No page or HTTP code changes.

**The logs bypass the seam.** They are bytes, not verbs. `--log-dir DIR` (the directory
`storaged` writes; no default) is opened read-only by `statusd`. Without it the log routes
answer 503 `unavailable`. Labeling needs nothing from `statusd`: every record in a segment
has its own `src` byte, so a `synth` or `replay` log says so wherever it is read.

**Routes** (HTTP/1.1, GET only, `Connection: close`, single-threaded `poll()`):

| Route | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `/` | static page (HTML+CSS+JS embedded as C strings, no CDN: device is offline) |
| `/api/status` `/api/verdicts` `/api/series?pid=0C&from=..&to=..` `/api/faults` | the verb reply converted to JSON (done) |
| `/api/logs` | JSON list of segments: `name`, `bytes`, `mtime_s`, newest last |
| `/logs/log-<16 hex>.cwr` | that segment's bytes, `application/octet-stream` |
| anything else | 404; non-GET 405; oversized/malformed request 400 |

**Segment serving rules.**
- Name must match `log-` + 16 lowercase hex + `.cwr` exactly. Anything else is a 400
  before any filesystem call; a name that matches but is absent is a 404. No query.
- Open with `openat(dirfd, name, O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC|O_NOFOLLOW)`, `fstat` it, require a
  regular file. The length sent is the size at open; bytes appended later are not sent, so
  `Content-Length` stays true while `storaged` writes the open segment.
- The open segment may end in an uncommitted batch or a torn record. That is served as it
  is; the decoder drops it exactly as recovery does (everything after the last COMMIT).
- `statusd` is read-only on the directory and never writes, renames or deletes.

**Page.** Four panels plus a Logs list, polled every 2 s with `fetch`: Latest values,
Verdicts/faults, Process health (supervisor/obdd/storaged/analyzed/statusd: up/down,
uptime, restarts, RSS, ring depth), Trends (inline-SVG sparklines through one
`drawSeries`), and Logs (`/api/logs`, one `<a download>` per segment). A persistent banner
shows **SYNTHETIC DATA** whenever any row has `src=synth` (CLAUDE.md §2.7). Read-only.

**Binding.** Default `127.0.0.1:8080` for development; `--bind ADDR` / `--port N` for the
AP address on the Pi (never `0.0.0.0`). Logs via `common/log.h`, every syscall error
logged, `goto`-cleanup, every allocation checked, no VLAs. SIGTERM exits 0, heartbeat via
`log_heartbeat` (§2.6).

## Files

Done (steps 1-5): `http.c`, `kv.c`, `json.c`, `synth_source.c`, `server.c`, `route.c`,
`statusd_main.c` and their tests.

New for the log work (under `src/interface/` unless noted):
- `logs.c` + `include/interface/logs.h`: segment-name check, directory listing, open one segment.
- `server.c`/`server.h` edit: a response whose body is a file descriptor, streamed.
- `route.c` edit: `/api/logs`, `/logs/<name>`; `statusd_main.c` edit: `--log-dir`.
- `tools/cwr2csv.py` + `tests/tools/test_cwr2csv.py` + a committed golden segment.
- Tests: `tests/test_logs.c`, additions to `test_server.c`, `test_route.c`, `test_statusd.c`.
- `page.c` (step 7): embedded HTML/CSS/JS.

Edits: `docs/DECISIONS.md` (new ⚠️ UNREVIEWED decision, next free ID, in the same commit as
the code that enacts it, plus its Review Queue row; D-045's "What is already coded" says
the CSV report follows, fix that sentence in the same commit); `docs/DESIGN.md` §1 note;
`docs/milestones.md` open boxes only; then `python3 tools/board_sync.py`. `tests/boundary/`:
no rule change expected (no new `AF_INET`); run it to confirm.

## Commit sequence (CLAUDE.md §7; branch `lance/m3/statusd`, draft PR opened already)

Session is **Lance's**. Stage explicit paths only. Tests lead: written first and seen
failing. Each commit builds and passes `make`, `make test`, `make asan` on its own.

Steps 1-5 are committed (HTTP layer; reply-line parser; JSON writer; synth source behind
the seam; `statusd` served and built). Remaining:

**6a. `M3 interface: list and open log segments`**
`logs.c`, `logs.h`, `tests/test_logs.c`. No sockets, no server. Methods:

| Method | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `bool logs_name_ok(const char *name)` | True only for `log-` + 16 lowercase hex + `.cwr`, nothing before or after. No `/`, no `..`, no NUL tricks, no uppercase. |
| `int logs_open_dir(const char *path)` | `open(O_RDONLY\|O_DIRECTORY\|O_CLOEXEC)`; returns the fd, or -1 having logged. Called once at startup. |
| `int logs_list(int dirfd, log_entry_t *out, size_t max, size_t *n)` | Reads the directory, keeps names that pass `logs_name_ok`, `fstatat`s each (regular files only, symlinks skipped), sorts by name (names are zero-padded hex, so name order is seq order). Fails -1 if there are more than `max`, rather than listing some. |
| `int logs_open_segment(int dirfd, const char *name, off_t *size)` | Re-checks `logs_name_ok`, `openat(O_RDONLY\|O_CLOEXEC\|O_NOFOLLOW)`, `fstat`, requires `S_ISREG`; returns the fd and the size at open, or -1 with `errno`-based reason (ENOENT vs refusal) distinguishable by return code. |

Tests: good and bad names (traversal, uppercase hex, short hex, trailing junk, embedded NUL
by length); listing sorts and ignores strangers (`README`, `log-x.cwr`, a directory named
like a segment, a symlink named like a segment); open refuses a symlink; size is the size
at open even if the file grows afterward; empty directory lists zero.

**6b. `M3 interface: stream a file body from the server`**
`server.c`, `server.h`, additions to `tests/test_server.c`. Separate because it changes
the connection state machine, which is the riskiest code in `statusd`. Today a response is
at most 48 KB, in memory, with one 5 s deadline for the whole write; a 16 MB segment fits
neither. Changes:
- `server_response_t` gains `int body_fd` (-1 default) and `uint64_t body_len64`; a handler
  that sets it transfers ownership of the fd to the server, which closes it on every exit
  path (done, client gone, timeout, server_close).
- New state `CONN_STREAMING`: send the head, then `pread` up to the buffer size and `send`
  until `body_len64` bytes are out. Never blocks (non-blocking socket, `POLLOUT`), so the
  other connections keep being served during a download.
- Deadlines: the existing "no trickling" rule stays for requests and ordinary responses.
  A stream gets an **idle** deadline (`SERVER_DEADLINE_MS` with no byte accepted by the
  client) and a **total** cap (`SERVER_STREAM_MAX_MS`, 10 minutes) so a client that
  trickles cannot hold one of the 4 slots forever.
- If `pread` returns fewer bytes than promised (file truncated underneath us), the head is
  already sent, so the only honest move is to close the connection and log an ERROR; the
  client sees a short body against `Content-Length`.
Tests (fake clock, no sleeping): a 3 MB file arrives byte-identical; a second client is
answered while the first is mid-stream; a client that stops reading hits the idle
deadline and the slot frees; a client that reads 1 byte per interval hits the total cap;
a client that closes mid-stream frees the slot; the fd count (`/proc/self/fd`) returns to
baseline after each case; a file truncated mid-stream closes the connection and logs.

**6c. `M3 interface: serve log segments at /logs and list them at /api/logs`**
`route.c`, `route.h`, `statusd_main.c`, `tests/test_route.c`, `tests/test_statusd.c`, and
the new decision (see below) with its Review Queue row, plus the D-045 sentence fix, in
this commit (CLAUDE.md §7.7). `--log-dir`, opened at startup; routes as in the table. No
`--log-dir`: both routes 503 `unavailable`. `/api/logs` is `{"ok":true,"records":[{"tag":
"segment","name":...,"bytes":...,"mtime_s":...}]}`, the same envelope as every other API
route, so the page needs no special case. Tests: listing matches the directory; download
is byte-identical to the file; traversal attempts get 400 and never touch the filesystem
(`..%2f`, `%00`, `log-<16hex>.cwr/..`, an absolute path); a symlinked segment is a 404; a
query is a 400; an open segment that grows during a download still delivers exactly the
promised length; 503 without `--log-dir`; `statusd` fd count is still listener plus the
directory (update the existing `open_fds == 1` check deliberately, in this commit, with
the reason).

**6d. `M3 tools: decode a log segment to CSV`**
`tools/cwr2csv.py`, `tests/tools/test_cwr2csv.py`, a golden segment under
`tests/tools/fixtures/` written once by the C writer, and a C test that the same file
still decodes with `rec_decode` (so both languages are pinned to the same bytes, and a
format change in `record.h` fails a test instead of silently breaking the tool). Runs on
a laptop, never on the box. Columns: `seq,boot_id,wall_ns,mono_ns,src,kind,mode,pid,value,
raw_hex,flags,text`, `src` always present (§2.7), Python `csv` module for quoting. Verifies
every CRC; keeps only records up to the last COMMIT (as recovery does) and says on stderr
how many it dropped; exits nonzero on a bad record before the tail. Python stays in
`tools/` (§2.5); the graded mechanisms (storage, serving) stay in C.

**7. `M3 interface: add the status page`**
`page.c`: embedded HTML/CSS/JS, vanilla. Panels as above, Logs panel from `/api/logs`
with `<a download>` links (the file name is the download name, so no
`Content-Disposition` change to `http.c`). All charts go through one `drawSeries(el, ts,
ys)` so uPlot can replace it later. SYNTHETIC DATA banner driven by `src`. Delete the
placeholder page and its check in `tests/test_route.c`. Test: `/` returns the page with
the banner element and the script; manual check in a phone-width browser.

**8. `M3 docs: board boxes for the real source, supervisor spawn and the HTML report`**
`docs/milestones.md` open boxes only: `ctlsource` (replace the synth source with a
ctl.sock client), `statusspawn` (supervisor starts statusd and passes `--log-dir`),
`uplot`, and a note on `report` that its CSV half is now the log download plus
`cwr2csv.py` (D-028 amendment goes in the decision below). DESIGN.md §1 note, then
`python3 tools/board_sync.py`. Does not tick `statusd` or `report`; a human does that.

PR title follows the lead claim of 5; the PR was opened as a draft at commit 1, and its
body gets the log work added at 6c.

## The decision to draft in 6c (⚠️ UNREVIEWED, next free ID)

"`statusd` may read the log directory, read-only, and serve segment files unparsed."
It **bends** two things, so it must be said plainly and a human must say yes:
- D-043 (B.11): "builds every page and report from the same control-socket verbs, so it
  holds no state of its own." Still true of state; but it is no longer *only* verbs.
- D-031's rule that only the process holding the answer reads the log, and B.11's rejected
  alternative ("`obdctl` reading the log files itself"). The carve-out: `statusd` copies
  bytes and never interprets one; `storaged` remains the only parser. It also **amends
  D-028**: the report's CSV is produced off the box from the served segments.
Check before coding 6c: confirm in `docs/DECISIONS.md` whether D-031 or B.11 is 🔒 LOCKED.
If either is, stop and get a human yes before the commit (CLAUDE.md §0).

## Verification

- `make`, `make test` (includes `boundary`, `boardcheck`, `toolcheck`), `make asan`: all
  green, output pasted in the PR. `python` is not on PATH here, only `python3`.
- Manual: `make run-status` with `--log-dir` on a directory holding a real segment (from
  `storaged` or the test writer); `curl /api/logs`; `curl -o x.cwr /logs/<name>` and
  `cmp` against the original; `python3 tools/cwr2csv.py x.cwr | head`; a 16 MB segment
  over loopback while the page keeps refreshing in a browser; bad inputs (`printf
  'GARBAGE\r\n\r\n' | nc 127.0.0.1 8080`, a 100 KB header, a slow client, `curl
  /logs/..%2f..%2fetc%2fpasswd`) get 400/closed without crashing.
- `kill -TERM` exits 0, also mid-download; `kill -9` leaves no stray fds (`ls
  /proc/<pid>/fd` before/after).
- Network unplugged on loopback: `ss -tp` shows only the listener.

## Least sure about / for review

- The new decision reopens a separation D-031 drew on purpose; the narrow "bytes, never
  parsed" wording is mine and needs a human's judgment.
- Streaming adds a state to a loop that had two. 6b is the commit to read slowest.
- A raw `.cwr` is not readable on a phone; the owner needs a laptop and `cwr2csv.py`. If
  phone-readable data matters, the follow-up is a transient on-the-fly decode streamed as
  CSV from the segment (nothing stored twice), not this PR.
- The open segment is served with a possibly uncommitted tail; correct only because the
  decoder drops it. A closed-only rule would be simpler but useless: at 1.4 KB/s a 16 MB
  segment is about 3 hours of driving.
- Confirm no VIN or other identifier can appear in event text (D-033 hashes the VIN for
  the JSONL logs; segments are served as they are).
- The "latest values" strip was not in the chosen scope; cheap to drop.
- The new decision is ⚠️ UNREVIEWED until Camden or Lance signs it.

`phoneview` (M4) and `report` (M3) are the later content items. Today there is no server
code at all. The goal now: a working site showing faults/verdicts, process health, trends
and a CSV report, fed by **synthetic** values behind a seam, so the real OBD2/analysis data
plugs in later with no page changes.

Decisions already made with the user: server in **C** (matches D-043); **standalone
binary now**, supervisor spawning stays with `supfork` (#41); page scope = faults list,
process health, trends + CSV. A small "latest values" strip is included because trends are
meaningless without current readings (flag in review if unwanted).

## Design

**The seam (the whole point).** D-043 says the page is built from control-socket verbs
(`status`, `verdicts`, `series`, `faults`; reply = `key=value` lines then `ok`). So
`statusd` talks to a *source* with one function: `source_query(verb, args, out_buf)`
returning exactly that D-043 text. Two implementations behind one header:
- `synth_source.c` (now): deterministic fake data, every record `src=synth`.
- `ctl_source.c` (later, not in this PR): connects to `/run/carwatch/ctl.sock`.
Swapping = one line in `statusd_main.c`. No page or HTTP code changes.

**Routes** (HTTP/1.1, GET only, `Connection: close`, single-threaded `poll()`):

| Route | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `/` | static page (HTML+CSS+JS embedded as C strings, no CDN: device is offline) |
| `/api/status` `/api/verdicts` `/api/series?pid=0C&from=..&to=..` `/api/faults` | the verb reply converted to JSON |
| `/report.csv` | CSV built from `series`+`verdicts`, `src` column on every row |
| anything else | 404; non-GET 405; oversized/malformed request 400 |

**Page.** Four panels, polled every 2 s with `fetch`: Latest values, Verdicts/faults
(active vs. past, fault area, cooperating sensors, residual), Process health
(supervisor/obdd/storaged/analyzed/statusd: up/down, uptime, restarts, RSS, ring depth),
Trends (inline-SVG sparklines per PID, drawn by ~60 lines of vanilla JS; no libraries).
A persistent banner shows **SYNTHETIC DATA** whenever any row has `src=synth` (CLAUDE.md
§2.7). Link to `/report.csv`. Read-only, no forms.

**Binding.** Default `127.0.0.1:8080` for development; `--bind ADDR` / `--port N` for the
AP address on the Pi (never defaults to `0.0.0.0`). Logs via `common/log.h`
(`log_init("statusd", ...)`, `log_set_src(SRC_SYNTH)`), every syscall error logged,
`goto`-cleanup, every allocation checked, no VLAs. SIGTERM exits 0 cleanly, heartbeat
via `log_heartbeat` so it is supervisable later (§2.6).

## Files

New (all under `src/interface/` unless noted):
- `statusd_main.c`: arg parsing, listen socket, poll loop, signals.
- `http.c` + `include/interface/http.h`: request-line parser and response writer (bounded buffers, header size cap, timeouts on slow clients).
- `source.h`: the seam; `synth_source.c`: fake data (sine/random-walk RPM, speed, coolant, load, probe temp; 2 fake verdicts e.g. "cooling" and "intake/vacuum"; 5 fake process rows).
- `kv.c` + `include/interface/kv.h`: parse D-043 `key=value` reply lines; `json.c`: tiny JSON writer with escaping.
- `page.c`: embedded HTML/CSS/JS (or `src/interface/page/*.html` + a `make`-time generator, only if the embedded string gets unwieldy).
- Tests (same commit as each unit): `tests/test_http.c` (good/bad/oversized/partial requests), `tests/test_kv.c`, `tests/test_json.c` (escaping), `tests/test_statusd.c` (start on an ephemeral port, GET each route, check 200/404/405, `src=synth` present, CSV header).

Edits:
- `Makefile`: add `statusd` to `DAEMONS`, link rule `$(BIN)/statusd: $(BUILD)/src/interface/statusd_main.o $(COMMON_OBJ)`; change `COMMON_SRC` filter from `%/main.c` to `%main.c` so `statusd_main.c` stays out of the library; add `make run-status`.
- `docs/DECISIONS.md`: new ⚠️ UNREVIEWED entry (next free ID, "synthetic source seam; `statusd` standalone until `supfork`") **in the same commit as the code**, plus Review Queue row; `docs/DESIGN.md` §1 note; `docs/milestones.md`: add open boxes only (e.g. `ctlsource`: replace synth source with ctl.sock client; `statusspawn`: supervisor spawns statusd), never tick `statusd`. Then `python tools/board_sync.py`.
- `tests/boundary/`: no rule change expected (AF_INET only in `src/interface/` already passes); run it to confirm, and add a `good_` case only if the checker needs one.

Reuse: `common/log.h` (logging, `data_src_t`/`SRC_SYNTH`, `log_heartbeat`); `Makefile` test globbing picks up new `tests/test_*.c` automatically; existing `tools/obdsim.py` is *not* used (that emulates the adapter, a different layer).

## Commit sequence (CLAUDE.md §7; branch `lance/m3/statusd`, draft PR at first commit)

Session is **Lance's**. Branch from fresh `main` before any edit. Stage explicit paths only.
Tests lead: in each commit the test is written first and seen failing. Each commit builds
and passes `make`, `make test`, `make asan` on its own.

1. `M3 interface: parse HTTP requests and write responses`
   `http.c`, `include/interface/http.h`, `tests/test_http.c`. Pure functions, no sockets:
   parse a request line (GET only) and headers out of a byte buffer, reporting
   incomplete / bad / too large; format a response with status, `Content-Type`,
   `Content-Length`. Tests: good GET, partial read, bad method (405), garbage (400),
   header over the size cap, embedded NULs, path with `..`.
2. `M3 interface: parse control-socket reply lines`
   `kv.c`, `include/interface/kv.h`, `tests/test_kv.c`. Reads the D-043 reply format
   (`key=value` lines, then `ok` or `err <code> <reason>`) into a bounded struct. Tests:
   normal reply, `err`, missing terminator, over-long line, empty value.
3. `M3 interface: write JSON with escaping`
   `json.c`, `include/interface/json.h`, `tests/test_json.c`. Tiny writer into a bounded
   buffer: objects, arrays, strings with quote/backslash/control-char escaping, and a
   truncation error rather than overflow. Separate from 2 because it is a different
   yes/no: the parser reads, this writes.
4. `M3 interface: synthetic data source behind the control-socket seam`
   `source.h`, `synth_source.c`, `tests/test_synth_source.c`. `source_query(verb, args,
   out)` returns D-043-format text for `status`, `verdicts`, `series`, `faults`. Values
   are deterministic from a time argument (so tests are exact) and every row carries
   `src=synth`. Test asserts that no reply line lacks `src=synth` and that replies parse
   with commit 2's parser.
5. `M3 interface: serve the status API from statusd`
   `statusd_main.c`, Makefile (`statusd` in `DAEMONS`, `%main.c` filter, `make
   run-status`), `tests/test_statusd.c`, and draft decision D-045 (own server, no
   libraries, synth seam, standalone until `supfork`; uPlot deferred) with its
   Review Queue row, in this same commit (CLAUDE.md §7.7). `poll()` loop, `--bind` /
   `--port`, per-connection deadline, SIGTERM exits 0, `log_heartbeat`. Routes
   `/api/status|verdicts|series|faults` via commits 1-4; `/` is a one-line placeholder.
   Likely over 400 lines; `WHY` will say it is the first commit that is a runnable
   process and the decision cannot precede it.
6. `M3 interface: add the CSV report route`
   `/report.csv` built from `series` + `verdicts`, `src` column on every row, header row,
   CSV field quoting. Tests extend `test_statusd.c`. Separate because it is its own
   output format with its own quoting rules (D-028).
7. `M3 interface: add the status page`
   `page.c`: embedded HTML/CSS/JS, vanilla. Panels: latest values, verdicts/faults,
   process health, trends. All charts go through one `drawSeries(el, ts, ys)` function
   (SVG polyline) so uPlot can replace it later. Persistent SYNTHETIC DATA banner driven
   by the `src` field. Test: `/` returns the page with the banner element and the
   script; manual check in a phone-width browser.
8. `M3 docs: board boxes for the real source and supervisor spawn`
   `docs/milestones.md` open boxes (`ctlsource`: replace the synth source with a
   ctl.sock client; `statusspawn`: supervisor starts statusd; `uplot`: revisit charting
   at phoneview), a DESIGN.md §1 note, then `python3 tools/board_sync.py`. Does not tick
   `statusd`; a human does that.

PR title follows commit 5's lead claim, opened as a draft at commit 1.

## Verification

- `make`, `make test` (includes `boundary`, `boardcheck`, `toolcheck`), `make asan`: all green, output pasted in the PR. Note `python` is not on PATH here (only `python3`), so run `python3 tools/board_sync.py`.
- Manual: `make run-status`, open `http://127.0.0.1:8080/`; confirm the SYNTHETIC banner, panels update every 2 s, `curl -i` each route, `curl /report.csv | head` shows `src=synth` on every row, bad inputs (`printf 'GARBAGE\r\n\r\n' | nc 127.0.0.1 8080`, a 100 KB header, a slow client) get 400/closed without crashing.
- `kill -TERM` exits 0; `kill -9` leaves no stray fds (`ls /proc/<pid>/fd` before/after).
- Run with the network unplugged on loopback to confirm no outbound calls (`ss -tp` shows only the listener).

## Least sure about / for review

- Single-threaded `poll()` is enough for one phone; a slow client is handled by a per-connection deadline, which needs a test.
- Embedded page strings are reviewable but awkward; split to files if it passes ~300 lines.
- The "latest values" strip was not in the chosen scope; cheap to drop.
- The new decision is ⚠️ UNREVIEWED until Camden or Lance signs it.

These are layouts for step 7. All of them are one page of vanilla HTML, CSS and JS embedded in C. They poll every 2 s, draw charts through `drawSeries`, and use a phone-width-first layout with no libraries or CDN. They all keep the same pieces: a persistent SYNTHETIC DATA banner, a dummy "Download logs" button, and read-only content.

## A. Single scrolling dashboard of cards

A sticky banner sits at the top, with the SYNTHETIC strip in amber. Below it is a big status header: a coloured dot and one sentence such as "All normal" or "1 active issue: cooling". The dot mirrors the box's tri-color light (D-027). Cards stack in one column:
1. Latest values: a 2×3 grid of big numbers (RPM, speed, coolant, load, trims, probe) with units.
2. Verdicts: active ones first, each showing area, cooperating sensors, residual and when it began. Ended ones are greyed below.
3. Trends: one sparkline per PID with its current value at the right.
4. Process health: a compact table of up/down, uptime, restarts and RSS.
5. Footer with the Download button.

**Advantages:**
- It's the simplest to build and test, and the closest to the plan.
- Nothing is hidden behind a tap.
- It works on a phone and on a laptop (two columns past about 900 px).
- Easy to review.

**Drawbacks:**
- It's a long scroll on a phone, so trends are far from the verdicts that explain them.

## B. Tabbed or bottom-nav app feel

There's a persistent top header with the banner and the status dot. A bottom bar has four tabs: **Now** (latest values plus active verdicts), **Trends**, **Faults** (verdict and event history), **System** (process health, rings, link state, Download button). Only one tab's content is shown at a time.

**Advantages:**
- Short screens, big touch targets, and it feels like an app, which suits a phone in a car.
- Polling can pause for hidden tabs, which saves work on the Pi.

**Drawbacks:**
- It adds routing and state code in JS. Without the History API, the back button misbehaves.
- Fewer things are visible at once.
- It's harder to eyeball from a screenshot during the defense.

## C. Health-first "traffic light" page with drill-down

The top two thirds of the screen is one large element in the colour of the box's light: green with "Learning, normal", amber with "Watching: cooling drifting", or red with "Issue in the car" or "Issue in the box". The report already has to say which side the fault is on (D-027). Under it is a one-line summary per area. Tapping a row expands its detail inline: the verdict, its sensors, and a sparkline of just the PIDs involved.

**Advantages:**
- It matches the product claim, because the owner sees what's wrong before any number.
- The least reading for someone who isn't a mechanic.
- Trends appear only when relevant.

**Drawbacks:**
- Latest values and process health are tucked away, which weakens the demo of the data underneath.
- A grader wanting to see everything needs extra taps.
- The view depends most on the real analysis output, which doesn't exist yet. With synth data it can look staged.

## D. Dense "instrument cluster" board

A dark, high-contrast layout (readable at night in a car), laid out as a grid of tiles that reflows from 1 to 3 columns. Each tile is a live gauge: a large value, a unit, a sparkline behind it, and a border that turns amber or red when that signal is part of an active verdict. Verdicts run along the top as chips. Process health is a thin strip of dots at the bottom, with a number on hover or tap.

**Advantages:**
- The most striking in a demo, and trends and values are in the same place.
- Strong in dark mode and glanceable.
- Mapping a verdict to its signals visually shows the "two cooperating sensors" idea.

**Drawbacks:**
- The most CSS and the most JS, so it's the one most likely to pass the 300-line embedded-string limit and need split files.
- Process health and event history get less room.
- Colour alone can't carry meaning, so it needs text labels for accessibility.

## Choosing

This is how design B would work with a status bar that carries the health colour. I haven't written anything.

## The core idea

The bar is the only thing on the page whose colour means "health". The tabs underneath can be calm, dense or empty, because the one question "is anything wrong?" is answered by a bar that never scrolls and never hides. That is what makes tabs safe here. Normally tabs bury information, but nothing that matters can hide behind one.

## The bar

- **Position:** it's fixed at the top, about 56 px tall, and full width.
- **Colour:** green means normal and red means an issue.
- **Text:** a glyph plus a headline in large type, so colour isn't the only signal (colour-blind owners, sun glare). Examples:
  - "✓ Normal"
  - "! Car: cooling system"
  - "! Box: obdd is down"
- **Right side:** a small "updated 2 s ago", plus a "+1 more" count when there are several reasons.
- **Tap:** it opens the Faults tab, scrolled to the reasons.
- **Browser chrome:** `<meta name="theme-color">` is set to the same colour on each update, so the phone's address bar matches. `document.title` gets a "!" prefix when red, which helps with a tab left in the background.
- **Synthetic banner:** it's a separate thin amber strip under the bar, not folded into it. The bar's colour should only ever mean health, and the banner (CLAUDE.md §2.7) must not be dismissible.

## A third state: grey, "can't reach the box"

You described green and red, but the page needs a third state or it will lie. The box is off whenever the car is (D-024), and a phone on its Wi-Fi drops often. A page that last saw green and then lost contact would keep showing green.

- **Grey on 3 missed polls:** after three failed or timed-out polls (about 6 s), the bar turns grey and reads "Can't reach the box · last seen 14:02".
- **Three misses, not one:** one miss is a Wi-Fi hiccup, so this stops the bar flickering.
- **Never stale green:** only a successful poll can paint green.
- **Connecting:** the same grey state covers first load ("Connecting…").
- **Pulse:** the bar flashes subtly on each successful poll, echoing the pulsing LED (D-027). A frozen page then looks frozen and can't look alive.

## How red is decided

One pure function, `computeHealth(status, verdicts)`, returns `{level, side, headline, reasons[]}`. Rules, from the data the API already returns:

| Condition | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Any verdict with `state="active"` | Red, **car**, headline names the `area`. |
| Any `proc` not `up`, or a ring with `overruns>0` | Red, **box**. |
| `verdicts` or `status` answering 503 `unavailable` | Red, **box** ("analysis unavailable"). A missing analyzer is a box problem, not a clean bill of health. |
| Otherwise | Green. |

- **Box or car:** D-027 says the report must say which side. Here it's in the headline text, not a third colour.
- **Several reasons:** the box side is listed first, because a broken box also makes car verdicts untrustworthy.
- **The synth `link` record already has a `light` field.** The light and the bar should agree. The real source could send that field and the page could render it directly, so there's one source of truth. Otherwise the C logic and the JS logic could drift apart. I'd decide this with the real source in mind.
- **Flicker:** `analyzed` already applies hysteresis to verdicts. I wouldn't add another latch for box faults, since a real process restart is worth seeing.

## The tabs

A bottom bar with four tabs, using hash routing (`#now`, `#trends`, `#faults`, `#system`). The back button works for free with `hashchange`. The History API isn't needed, so I'd retract the "routing is a drawback" point I made earlier.

| Tab | Content | Polls |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Now** | Big latest values in a grid, active verdicts below | status, verdicts, latest values |
| **Trends** | A chip row to pick one PID, a window selector (5 m, 30 m, 1 h), one large chart | series, one request |
| **Faults** | Active verdicts first, then ended ones, then the event timeline (detection, degradation, recovery) | faults |
| **System** | Process table, rings, dongle and probe, source mix, dummy Download button (disabled, "coming soon") | status |

- **Badges:** the Faults tab shows a red count of active verdicts. System shows a dot if a process is down. You can see where to look without opening anything.
- **Trends is better here than in a long scroll.** One chart gets the full width and a readable height, and the page fetches one series instead of seven.

## Polling

- **Always poll:** `/api/status` and `/api/verdicts` every 2 s, because the bar needs them.
- **Per tab:** the active tab adds its own request. Hidden tabs add nothing.
- **Sequential, not parallel:** `statusd` is single-threaded with 4 connection slots, so the page must not flood it. One request at a time, chained with `setTimeout` (not `setInterval`, which piles up when the box is slow).
- **Per-request timeout:** each fetch has a 3 s timeout via `AbortController`.
- **Background tabs:** polling pauses on `visibilitychange` and refreshes immediately on return.

## Real design problem: latest values

The Now tab needs the most recent value of each signal, and D-043 has no "latest" verb. Today the choices are:
1. **Seven `series` calls per cycle,** each with a 10 s window. That's too heavy for a 2 s poll.
2. **Poll them every 5 s** instead of 2 s. This is acceptable for the dummy phase.
3. **Add a `latest` verb** to the seam. This is the right long-term answer, but it changes D-043 and needs a decision.

I'd do option 2 now and put option 3 on the board as an open box.

## Code shape (~300 lines of JS)

- `api(path)` is a fetch wrapper with a timeout. It returns parsed JSON or throws.
- `poll()` runs the chained loop and updates the shared state object.
- `computeHealth()` is the pure function above.
- `renderBar()`, `renderNow()`, `renderTrends()`, `renderFaults()` and `renderSystem()` each take state and update their DOM.
- `drawSeries(el, ts, ys)` is the one chart function (the uPlot seam).
- `route()` handles the hash and toggles `hidden` on panels.
- All values go in with `textContent`, never `innerHTML`. The data is ASCII-clean, but a source value should never be able to inject markup.

## Weaknesses

- **Untested logic:** the C tests can check the page contains the right element ids, but `computeHealth` is JavaScript and nothing in the current suite runs JS. Options:
  - keep it very small and check it by hand;
  - add a Node-based test (the project allows Python in `tools/` and `tests/tools/`, but a JS test runner would be new);
  - put the health rules server-side as a `health` field in the C JSON. That is testable but moves logic into `route.c`, which edges toward double-defining the light's rules.
- **Hidden detail:** a reviewer sees one tab at a time, so screenshots for the defense take four shots.
- **Bar colour on synth data:** with the dummy source, the verdicts list shows one active cooling verdict, so the bar would sit red the whole time. That's accurate to the data, but it makes a poor default demo. We could add a `?demo=ok` toggle to the synth source, or a clean dataset at certain times.

## Questions for you

1. Are you OK with the grey third state? I think it's required for honesty, not optional.
2. Should the light and the bar be driven by the source's `light` field (one truth), or should the page compute health itself?
3. For the dummy phase, which should the synth source default to: green, red, or alternating on a timer so both are visible?
I am a bit confused on how the box could properly report its status, as the website is hosted on the box itself.

You're right: a page served by the box can't report that the box has died. The design handles this by dividing failures by who can observe them. Nothing on the box has to report its own death.

## Who watches whom

| What fails | Who notices | What the page shows |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A worker dies (`obdd`, `analyzed`, `storaged`) | The supervisor, which started it. `statusd` is still running and asks the supervisor over `ctl.sock`. | **Red**, "Box: obdd is down". This works normally. |
| The supervisor dies | `statusd`, because its `ctl.sock` connection fails. systemd also restarts the supervisor (`Restart=always`). | **Red**. `statusd` is alive and returns 503 `unavailable`, which the page maps to "Box: supervisor unreachable". |
| `statusd` itself dies or hangs | **The phone.** The page is already loaded, and its polls fail or time out. | **Grey**, "Can't reach the box". |
| The whole box is off, or the phone is out of Wi-Fi range | The phone, again. | **Grey**, the same as above. |
| The car is off | The same as the row above, since the box is off whenever the car is (D-024). | **Grey**. |

The box can only report a failure to the page while `statusd` is alive. When `statusd` is gone, the only observer left is the page in the phone, which is already loaded and keeps running. That is why grey exists: it's the phone saying "I've stopped hearing from the box", not the box saying anything.

## What grey can't tell you

Grey can't distinguish a crashed `statusd`, a powered-off box, a car that's off and a phone that wandered out of range. They look the same from the phone's side. So the copy should say that: "Can't reach the box. It may be off, out of range, or not running." It should never say "Box is down".

The separate observer is the tri-color light (D-027), which doesn't depend on `statusd`. The failure table says that if the supervisor dies, the light freezes steady, which means "not running". So when the bar is grey and the box is in front of the owner, the light tells them whether the box is alive.

## A hung `statusd`

A process that is alive but stuck is the harder case. If `statusd` keeps answering but its data has stopped updating (a stuck source, for example), the page would keep showing the last good values. Two protections:
- **Age on every reply:** each `status` reply carries an age or timestamp (the supervisor's uptime, for instance). The page turns grey if that number stops advancing, even though HTTP still works.
- **Supervisor-side heartbeat:** the supervisor already expects children to heartbeat (CLAUDE.md §2.6). A wedged `statusd` is something the supervisor detects, not something the page needs to guess.

## After the fact

The box can't report a death in the moment, but it can report it afterwards. The log records `recovered` and `prev_end` at the next boot (D-025, D-034), so the Faults tab can show "the box restarted at 14:02 after an unclean end". The bar is for what's happening now. Faults is the history that survives the failure.

## How this changes the design

- **The bar logic doesn't change.** It still reports red from the data, and grey from poll failures.
- **Staleness needs a field.** The synth `status` reply doesn't carry an age field yet, only uptime values. We'd either rely on those or add a dedicated field. I'd flag it as an open question for the real source.
- **The grey copy matters.** The wording should name the limit honestly. I'd also point at the light in the grey state's help text.

/* statusd's routes (D-043, D-045): the handler that server.c calls for each request. It
 * maps a URL to one request line for the source, and turns the source's reply into JSON.
 * No sockets and no allocation; the 64 KB scratch buffer is the caller's.
 *
 *   /                      a placeholder page (see route.c: it is replaced by the real page)
 *   /api/status            status
 *   /api/verdicts          verdicts
 *   /api/faults            faults
 *   /api/series?pid=&from=&to=
 *                          series pid="..." from=... to=...
 *
 * Success is 200 with {"ok":true,"records":[{"tag":"proc","name":"obdd","pid":102,...}]},
 * each field typed as the source typed it (kv.h). Every refusal under /api/ is JSON too,
 * {"ok":false,"code":"usage","reason":"..."}, so the page can always parse a body.
 *
 * Whatever the URL carries is untrusted, and a request line is built from it. So query
 * keys are checked against a fixed list, each value must be 1 to 24 bytes of
 * [A-Za-z0-9:+.,_/-] after decoding, and anything else is a 400 that never reaches the
 * source. The routes take no other query: an unexpected key, a repeated one, or any query
 * on a route that takes none is a 400. A "+" in a URL decodes to a space, so a client that
 * means a plus sends %2B.
 */
#ifndef CARWATCH_ROUTE_H
#define CARWATCH_ROUTE_H

#include "interface/http.h"
#include "interface/server.h"
#include "interface/source.h"

#define ROUTE_REPLY_MAX  65536u

typedef struct {
    const source_t *src;
    char            reply[ROUTE_REPLY_MAX];   /* the source's text, before it becomes JSON */
} route_ctx_t;

/* A server_handler_t: ctx is a route_ctx_t whose src is set. */
void route_handle(void *ctx, const http_request_t *req, server_response_t *resp);

#endif

The page frame is built and served, with the tab system working. It's uncommitted, and I haven't checked it in a browser.

**What it does** ([page.c](src/interface/page.c), [page.h](include/interface/page.h))
- **Status bar:** a sticky bar at the top. It's a link to the Faults tab and shows a glyph, a headline and a small sub-line. The browser's `theme-color` and the tab title follow it.
- **Demo cycle:**
  - It cycles green, red, grey every 2 s.
  - It sits under the `TODO(ctlsource)` comment saying the real colour must come from the source's `light` field.
  - It's behind a single `DEMO_CYCLE` constant.
  - The bar says "DEMO: colors cycle every 2 s, this is not real health", so it can't be mistaken for real status.
- **Synthetic banner:** a non-dismissible amber strip under the bar. It's always shown for now.
- **Tabs:** Now, Trends, Faults and System sit in a bottom nav, chosen by the URL hash.
  - An unknown or empty hash falls back to Now, and the back button works.
  - The Now panel is visible even with scripting off, and a `<noscript>` note covers the rest.
  - Each panel holds a "not built yet" line.
- **Rules kept:** no external hosts or `innerHTML`, and it adapts to dark mode.
- **Placeholder removed:** `route.c` now serves the new page and the old placeholder string is gone. `route.h` and D-045's "what is already coded" paragraph are updated to match.

**Verification**
- **Tests:** I wrote `test_page` first and saw it fail. It checks the bar and banner, four panels and four tab links, the viewport tag, the offline rules and the demo marker. I updated the `/` check in `test_statusd.c` to match the new page.
- **Gates:** `make`, `make test` (136 Python tests plus every C test) and `make asan` all pass. I only pasted tails here, so the full output for the PR still needs capturing.
- **Live check:** `curl` against a running `statusd` returns a 200 with the 4,915-byte page.
- **Not checked:** the JavaScript has not run in a browser. Headless Firefox produced no screenshot and there's no Node here. Please open `make run-status` at `http://127.0.0.1:8080/` in a phone-width window and check four things:
  - the tabs switch;
  - the hash and back button work;
  - the bar cycles;
  - the layout looks right.
- **Skipped:** markdownlint and `board_sync --check` weren't run, because `npx` and `gh` aren't installed.

**Left for you**
- **Real poll-failure grey** isn't built yet. We discussed it behind the switch, but I kept this to the tab frame.
- **Commit:** I haven't committed. It would be one commit, `M3 interface: add the status page frame`. Say the word, or tell me if you'd rather split it.
- **Wording:** the D-045 edit is mine and the decision is still ⚠️ UNREVIEWED. Please check I worded it the way you want, since it says the report download was set aside.

content.content:
1001	client, TLS and a thread pool we would have to defend line by line, and Mongoose and
1002	CivetWeb contain HTTP *client* code that the rule "no HTTP client, ever" forbids. The
1003	parser is the one part that reads bytes a stranger on the Wi-Fi chose, so it is small,
1004	pure and tested against every refusal. GET-only keeps the rule to one sentence. A
1005	synthetic source lets the page be built and reviewed before the first drive, and
1006	`src=synth` keeps it from ever passing as data.
1007	
1008	**Cost.** The server uses Linux calls (`accept4`, `SOCK_NONBLOCK`, `MSG_NOSIGNAL`) and
1009	its tests read `/proc`, so `statusd` builds and is tested on the Pi and in CI but is not
1010	known to build with clang on macOS, which the Makefile mentions; nobody has tried. We
1011	own the parser's bugs. HEAD, keep-alive, ranges and TLS are unavailable, and
1012	adding HEAD later means a flag on every route to skip the body. The limits are Claude's
1013	choices, not measurements. The page has no tooltips, zoom or pan until a charting
1014	library is adopted, which needs its own decision (board item `uplot`, not yet added).
1015	
1016	**Order of commits.** §7.7 asks for a decision to share a commit with its code. Lance
1017	asked for this entry before the server code, so it is written in a docs commit after the
1018	HTTP layer's commits.
1019	
1020	**Alternatives rejected.** libmicrohttpd (an extra link-time dependency and threads we do
1021	not need); Mongoose and CivetWeb (client code, a license to read, a large surface); a
1022	Python server in `ui/` (D-028: an interpreter in the soak's memory plot). uPlot now: about
1023	50 KB of third-party code in the tree for charts the first cut does not need.
1024	
1025	---
1026	
1027	## C. Storage and data integrity
1028	
1029	### C.1 — Append-only, self-framing, CRC'd records 🔒
1030	
1031	`D-002/D` · Decided M0 · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
1032	
1033	*Extended 2026-10-21 by D-025 (§C.3), with Camden's explicit yes: records are written in
1034	committed batches, and baselines are saved in A/B checkpoint slots. Every rule below
1035	stays. Note 2026-10-27: the open sub-decision below is drafted as D-035 (§C.6).*
1036	
1037	Records are never rewritten in place. Each carries a magic number for resynchronization
1038	and a CRC32 over its whole body. Recovery scans from the last known-good offset, verifies
1039	CRCs, truncates the torn tail, and logs exactly what was lost.
1040	
1041	**Why.** We are interrupted mid-write by design, several times a day. Rewriting in place
1042	can destroy data that was previously correct; appending can only ever damage the last
1043	record. The CRC is what makes a torn record *detectable* rather than merely wrong — and
1044	wrong numbers you trust are more dangerous than missing numbers you know about.
1045	
1046	**Open sub-decision (M2, Lance):** fsync batch size and interval. There is no correct
1047	value, only one justifiable from user requirements. Document the argument in `docs/DESIGN.md`
1048	§5 before writing the code.
1049	
1050	### C.2 — Every record carries a provenance tag 🔒
1051	
1052	Decided M0 · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
1053	
1054	Every record and every log line carries `src = live | replay | synth`. Present in the
1055	format from day one, before any replay tooling exists.
1056	
1057	**Why.** Handout §5: replayed or synthesized data must be labeled everywhere it appears —
1058	logs, report, demo. Making it a mandatory field rather than a convention means it is
1059	structurally impossible to forget. Mislabeling synthesized data as live is the single
1060	integrity failure this course is best equipped to detect, and the worst trade available
1061	anywhere in it.
1062	
1063	### C.3 — Write-ahead transactions and A/B checkpoints ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
1064	
1065	`D-025` · Decided M2, 2026-10-21 · **By:** Camden (in session, extending 🔒 C.1) + Claude
1066	· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
1067	· **Extends:** 🔒 C.1, whose rules all stay: append-only, self-framing, CRC'd records,
1068	each carrying its `src` tag (C.2)
1069	
1070	**Decision.**
1071	
1072	- **Transactions (`storaged`).** `storaged` drains the ring into batches: a
1073	  `BEGIN(txn_id)` record, the sample records, a `COMMIT(txn_id)` record, then one
1074	  `fsync`. A batch is durable only once its `COMMIT` is on disk.
1075	- **Checkpoints (`analyzed`).** `analyzed` holds the learned per-bin baselines (D-031),
1076	  so it checkpoints them: now and then, a snapshot of the baselines plus the log offset
1077	  and the last committed `txn_id` it covers. There are two alternating slots, A and B,
1078	  each CRC'd and carrying a generation counter, so a checkpoint torn by a power cut never
1079	  destroys the previous good one.
1080	- **Recovery at boot.** `storaged` scans its log forward from the last offset it knows was
1081	  committed, verifying every CRC. The scan stops at the first bad record and truncates the
1082	  torn tail, and a batch with no `COMMIT` is truncated at its `BEGIN` (**undo**).
1083	  `analyzed` then loads the newest valid checkpoint slot and re-applies every committed
1084	  batch after its offset (**redo**), through the same code as live analysis. Both log
1085	  exactly what was recovered and what was lost, as counts and offsets.
1086	- **Every session starts with a boot record** that says whether the previous session
1087	  ended in a clean shutdown or was recovered. That needs a positive marker: a clean
1088	  shutdown ends the log with a shutdown record after its last `COMMIT`, because a crash
1089	  just after a `COMMIT` otherwise looks exactly like a clean end.
1090	
1091	**Why undo is only truncation.** Nothing is ever overwritten in place (C.1), so there is
1092	no before-image to restore: undo means discarding an uncommitted tail. Say so plainly at
1093	the defense, and do not claim an undo log the design does not need.
1094	
1095	**Extending a locked decision.** C.1 is 🔒. Camden approved this extension explicitly in
1096	the 2026-10-21 session (`docs/REVISION_PLAN.md` §1.1, P4), because it ties the storage
1097	layer to the logging and checkpoint techniques taught in class. C.1 stays 🔒 and gains a
1098	pointer.
1099	
1100	*Numbers revised 2026-10-26 by D-034 and D-035, before any review: a sample record is 56
1101	bytes, 2 to 5 MB per running hour, and the batch argument is D-035 (§C.6).*
1102	
1103	**Provisional numbers (estimates).** One `COMMIT` and one `fsync` per batch of about one
1104	second of samples. Records of about 48 bytes at 10 to 20 requests a second come to about
1105	1 KB/s, or about 3.5 MB per running hour. The worst loss from a power cut that beats the
1106	clean shutdown is then about one second of samples. The argument for the batch size is
1107	still written in `docs/DESIGN.md` §5 before the code, as C.1 requires (`fsync`).
1108	
1109	**Record format.** The new record kinds (transaction begin and commit, boot, clean
1110	shutdown) and a boot id in the header are settled in `recfmt`. The CRC known-answer test
1111	does not change.
1112	
1113	**Cost.** Recovery now spans two processes, so the crash tests (cut the file at every
1114	byte offset, then `expcrash` on the device) must cover both. Checkpoint frequency trades
1115	write load against redo time at boot.
1116	
1117	### C.4 — Drive captures are JSONL from a Python tool, VIN hashed ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
1118	
1119	`D-033` · Decided M2, 2026-10-26 · **By:** Camden (in session) + Claude
1120	· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
1121	
1122	**Decision.** Until `obdd` exists, real-car data is collected by `tools/obdlog.py`, run on
1123	Camden's Mac (or the Pi) against the OBDLink LX. It writes one file per session,
1124	`data/drive-<time>-<src>.jsonl`, one JSON object per line: a `header` (adapter,
1125	protocol, battery voltage, VIN hash, PID list, tool and schema version), a `sample` per
1126	reply (`src`, `seq`, `t_mono`, `t_wall`, `pid`, raw hex, decoded value, unit), an `event`
1127	for every non-sample outcome (`no_data`, `timeout`, `link_lost`, `reconnected`, ...),
1128	optional `gps` lines and a `footer`. It polls every supported PID round-robin as fast as
1129	the adapter answers. Writes are append-only and fsync'd every 50 lines or 1 s. The VIN is
1130	shown on screen and stored only as the first 12 hex digits of its SHA-256. A session
1131	against `obdsim` is labeled `synth` on every line, because the simulator's reset banner
1132	says `SIM`. *The `sample` record and the round-robin are amended in draft 2026-10-27
1133	by D-044 (§C.8).*
1134	
1135	**Why.** Camden, 2026-10-26: the first drive must log everything the car will answer so
1136	the data can be studied before the pipeline is designed around it. JSONL is readable by
1137	eye and by any analysis tool; the raw hex beside the decoded value means a decoding bug
1138	never costs data; event lines mean nothing is dropped silently (D-012). Camden chose
1139	hashing over storing the VIN.
1140	
1141	**A departure from D-012, stated.** D-012 budgets about 10 requests a second on a
1142	rate-limited schedule. This tool keeps D-012's one outstanding request, the core of its
1143	safety argument, but sends the next request as soon as the last is answered, because the
1144	first drives exist to measure what the adapter can do. The product's `obdd` keeps a rate
1145	limit, set from that measurement (`canreq`).
1146	
1147	**What this is not.** It is not mechanism D and not the on-disk format of `storaged`
1148	(`recfmt`, D-025). The product stays C (CLAUDE.md §2.4); this is a collection tool in
1149	`tools/` (§2.5). `tools/replay.py` will convert these files into the product's records,
1150	labeled `replay`.
1151	
1152	**Cost.** The hash is pseudonymization, not anonymity: a VIN has little entropy, so
1153	anyone holding candidate VINs can test them. Raw logs stay out of git (`data/` is
1154	ignored); only short excerpts are committed as evidence.
1155	
1156	### C.5 — The on-disk record format (draft) ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
1157	
1158	`D-034` · Drafted M2, 2026-10-26 · **By:** Claude, in Camden's session, without his review
1159	of the details · **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
1160	· **Finishes:** D-025's open `recfmt` item; keeps every rule of 🔒 C.1 and 🔒 C.2
1161	
1162	*Extended 2026-10-26 by D-037 (§B.9): a sample with `mode` 0x00 is from the box's own
1163	sensors; `pid` 0x01 is the DS18B20 probe, value in °C.*
1164	
1165	**Decision (draft).** `storaged` writes a log of self-framing records. Every multi-byte
1166	field is little-endian, the Pi's native order. Each record is a fixed header, a body whose
1167	layout depends on its kind, and a CRC32 (the existing `src/store/` CRC, known-answer
1168	tested) over everything before it, magic included.
1169	
1170	| Offset | Size | Field | Notes |
1171	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
1172	| 0 | 4 | `magic` | `0x31525743`, the bytes `CWR1`; the resynchronization point (C.1) |
1173	| 4 | 2 | `kind` | 1 sample, 2 begin, 3 commit, 4 boot, 5 shutdown, 6 event |
1174	| 6 | 2 | `body_len` | bytes of body; a reader rejects a length its kind does not allow |
1175	| 8 | 8 | `seq` | per log, never reused, continues across boots |
1176	| 16 | 8 | `mono_ns` | `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` at capture (samples) or at write (others) |
1177	| 24 | 8 | `wall_ns` | Unix time from the real-time clock (D-030) |
1178	| 32 | 1 | `src` | 1 `live`, 2 `replay`, 3 `synth` (C.2); 0 and any other value fail the record (D-040) |
1179	| 33 | 1 | `flags` | bit 0: wall time untrusted this session (D-030) |
1180	| 34 | 2 | reserved | zero |
1181	| 36 | 4 | `boot_id` | increments at every boot, so `mono_ns` is comparable only within one |
1182	| 40 | n | body | per kind, below |
1183	| 40 + n | 4 | `crc32` | over bytes 0 to 40 + n − 1 |
1184	
1185	| Kind | Body |
1186	| --- | --- |
1187	| sample | `mode` u8, `pid` u8, `raw_len` u8 (0 to 5), `raw[5]`, `value` f32 (12 bytes): the raw reply bytes are kept beside the decoded value so a decoding bug never costs data. Five bytes is the most a single-frame Mode 01 reply carries (0x64, for one, uses all five); a longer, multi-frame reply is stored as an event holding its hex |
1188	| begin | `txn_id` u64 |
1189	| commit | `txn_id` u64, `records` u32 (samples in the batch), reserved u32 |
1190	| boot | `prev_end` u8 (0 clean shutdown, 1 recovered, 2 first boot), reserved u8[3], `bytes_truncated` u32, `records_lost` u32 |
1191	| shutdown | `reason` u8 (1 source lost, 2 signal, 3 operator), reserved u8[7] |
1192	| event | `code` u16, `len` u16, then `len` bytes of text, at most 200; the codes are open until D-031's open item decides how verdicts and supervisor events reach storage |
1193	
1194	**Segments.** The log is a directory of segment files, `log-<first seq>.cwr`, each closed
1195	at about 16 MB (about four hours of driving at the D-025 rate). Recovery scans only the
1196	newest segment; retention deletes whole segments, oldest first, and never edits one.
1197	
1198	**Size and rate.** A sample record is 56 bytes. At 10 to 25 requests a second (D-012's
1199	budget up to what the unthrottled tool reaches on `obdsim`) that is 0.56 to 1.4 KB/s, or
1200	2 to 5 MB per running hour, plus a begin and a commit (112 bytes) per
1201	batch. D-025's estimate of 48 bytes becomes 56.
1202	
1203	**Why.** D-025 left the record kinds and the boot id to `recfmt`. The fields come straight
1204	from the decisions that need them: `src` (C.2), the boot id and untrusted-time flag
1205	(D-030), begin and commit (D-025), a boot record with a positive clean-shutdown marker
1206	(D-025), and raw bytes beside the value, which proved its worth in the logging tool
1207	(D-033). Fixed widths and a fixed header make the forward scan simple and the
1208	cut-at-every-byte test exhaustive. Segments keep recovery time bounded however long the
1209	box has run.
1210	
1211	**Open.** The event codes, and whether verdicts travel as events, wait on D-031's open
1212	item. The value field is f32: enough for every Mode 01 formula, but say so if a PID needs
1213	more.
1214	
1215	**Cost.** A format change touches `storaged`, `analyzed` and `tools/replay.py` at once
1216	(D-031). Little-endian is fixed in the file, so the log is not portable to a big-endian
1217	machine without a converter, which nothing here needs.
