82	## A. Hardware and interfaces
83	
84	### A.1 — The Pi reads OBD2 over a Bluetooth Classic adapter; USB is the fallback ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
85	
86	`D-019` · Decided M1, 2026-09-23 · **By:** Camden (in session) + Claude
87	· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
88	· **Supersedes:** D-015 (§G.4)
89	
90	*Pi power revised 2026-10-21 by D-024 (§A.6), before any review: the Pi is in a box fed
91	by the owner's USB-C charger, not wired to the car's USB. The adapter's key-off draw is
92	now board item `dongledrain`.*
93	
94	**Decision.** An **OBDLink LX** (STN chip, **Bluetooth Classic, Serial Port Profile**; not
95	BLE) plugs into the OBD2 port. The Pi, in the box (D-024), talks to it with
96	its built-in Bluetooth radio over RFCOMM. Provisioning pairs and trusts the adapter once,
97	binds it with `rfcomm bind` to `/dev/rfcomm0`, and a udev rule links that to **`/dev/obd`**,
98	so every consumer still opens `/dev/obd` and sends Mode 01 requests (D-012). No MCP2515, no
99	SPI, no CAN wiring, and no data cable in the cabin.
100	
101	**Raw CAN is still a stretch goal**: an MCP2515 on SPI, taken up only after mechanisms D
102	and E are implemented *and measured* (unchanged from D-015).
103	
104	**Why.** Camden's call, 2026-09-23: the goal is the simplest data path that works. The box
105	becomes one power cable; the adapter stays in the port. The protocol, the parsing and every
106	downstream design are the same as D-015, because an STN adapter speaks the same ELM327
107	command set over Bluetooth as over USB.
108	
109	*Note 2026-10-27: D-038 rewrote `make boundary`. `AF_BLUETOOTH` is now banned everywhere,
110	and Unix sockets are allowed through `src/ipc/uds.c`, so the reasoning below still holds.*
111	
112	**Why a tty and not our own Bluetooth socket.** Opening an RFCOMM socket from `obdd` would
113	put `socket()` in `src/obd/`, which `make boundary` forbids outside `src/interface/`
114	(CLAUDE.md §2.1). Letting the kernel's RFCOMM layer present a tty keeps the boundary check
115	meaningful and keeps `obdd` a plain serial reader.
116	
117	**What D-001 (§G.1) said against this, and why it no longer applies.** G.1 rejected a
118	Bluetooth ELM327 because it gives up interrupts and bus-level timing, taking mechanisms A,
119	B, C and F with it. D-015 already accepted exactly that loss for the USB adapter, and D-017
120	records what survives (D and E). Bluetooth costs no further mechanism.
121	
122	**Costs and risks.**
123	
124	- **Provisioning.** Pairing, trust and a persistent bind must survive reboots and every
125	  key-off (`scripts/provision_pi.sh`, board item `bench`).
126	- **A new failure mode.** The link can drop while the engine runs (adapter out of range,
127	  adapter asleep, radio interference). `obdd` sees a hangup on the tty and must reconnect
128	  with backoff, not crash-loop (`docs/DESIGN.md` §4, `supbackoff`).
129	- **One radio, two jobs.** The Pi 4's single Wi-Fi/Bluetooth chip also runs the phone
130	  access point (D-013). Coexistence is expected to work but is unmeasured: board item
131	  `btcoex`. Putting the access point on 5 GHz is the first mitigation to try.
132	- **Key-off draw.** The adapter still draws from OBD2 pin 16, live with the key off, and a
133	  Bluetooth adapter keeps a radio up. Its sleep behavior and key-off current are measured
134	  before it stays plugged in overnight (`dongledrain`).
135	
136	**Fallback.** The USB adapter of D-015 (§G.4) needs only a different udev rule to appear as
137	`/dev/obd`. If Bluetooth proves unreliable in the car, switching back is a provisioning
138	change, not a code change.
139	
140	### A.2 — Testbeds: Camden's 2008 Forester and Lance's 2015 CR-V ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
141	
142	`D-022` · Decided M2, 2026-10-21 · **By:** Camden (in session) + Claude
143	· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
144	· **Supersedes:** D-016 (§G.6) · **Amends:** the claim wording of D-021 (§E.1)
145	
146	**Decision.** Two cars are available as testbeds: Camden's **2008 Subaru Forester**
147	(non-turbo) and Lance's **2015 Honda CR-V EX-L** (D-007). Neither car is required of
148	anyone, and either partner tests wherever suits them. Every capture records which car it
149	came from.
150	
151	**Why.** Camden's call, 2026-10-21 (`docs/REVISION_PLAN.md` §1.1, P1): a car on Camden's
152	own schedule lets live capture start without waiting on anyone, and no document should
153	restrict where either partner tests. The device learns whichever car it is installed in,
154	so a second car costs no code.
155	
156	**The claim, reworded.** D-021's *"this CR-V"* becomes *"the car it is installed in"*
157	(§E.1). Results are reported per car and labeled with the car.
158	
159	**Cost.**
160	
161	- Each car needs its own PID survey (`pidforester`, `pidhonda`). The two sensor lists may
162	  differ, and the Forester's OBD protocol is not verified: a 2008 US car is expected to
163	  speak CAN (ISO 15765-4), but MAP, for one, may be absent.
164	- Baselines are per car. Two cars split the calendar time of normal driving unless one of
165	  them carries most of it.
166	
167	**Alternative rejected.** Keeping D-016 (the CR-V only): every live capture would wait on
168	one car's schedule.
169	
170	### A.3 — Honda year/model/engine ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
171	
172	`D-007` · **Owner:** Lance · **Tracked as:** GitHub issue `honda` (label `question`)
173	· **Answered:** 2026-09-21, by Camden in session · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
174	· **Blocks:** the PID survey, which sets the sensor list
175	
176	**Answer.** **2015 Honda CR-V EX-L.** By model year that is the 2015 refresh: 2.4 L
177	direct-injected four-cylinder (K24W) with a CVT. FWD or AWD is not yet recorded. The
178	engine and transmission are inferred from the model year, not read off the car — Lance
179	confirms against the VIN or the door-jamb sticker, then closes the issue.
180	
181	**What the answer changes.**
182	
183	- **No Honda Sensing on the EX-L** (it was Touring-only in 2015), so there is no
184	  lane-keep camera connector to tap. The OBD2 port is the tap point (**D-024**).
185	- **Oil pressure is expected to be a switch, not a sender** (inference from Honda
186	  practice). Under D-021 that only removes one sensor from the list; nothing depends on it.
187	- **The Honda has Maintenance Minder**, an oil-life estimate from how the engine has been
188	  run. We do not compete with it: carwatch watches every engine sensor for behavior that
189	  leaves this car's normal, which the Minder never measures.
190	
191	We still need, from the car itself, which Mode 01 PIDs the ECU actually supports: that
192	list is the model's input.
193	
194	**Action.** Run a supported-PID scan on the CR-V with the OBD2 adapter (D-019) —
195	a ten-minute experiment. Record in `docs/hardware/pid-survey.md`.
196	
197	### A.4 — Capture the schematic in KiCad; do not fabricate a PCB 🔒
198	
199	`D-009` · Decided M0 · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
200	
201	*Note 2026-10-27, not a reopening: the MCP2515 named below is now a stretch goal only
202	(D-019), and owners are per D-026. `make hwdocs` emits the schematic SVG, `bom.csv` and a
203	netlist; `BOM.md` and `wiring.md` are still written by hand and checked against them.*
204	
205	**Decision.** We draw the full schematic in KiCad (`electricalDrawing/`, KiCad 10, owned
206	by Lance) and treat it as the source of truth for wiring and the BOM. We do **not**
207	fabricate a custom PCB unless we take The Reach (handout §14). The empty `.kicad_pcb`
208	stays in the repo on purpose.
209	
210	**Why.** A custom board earns zero points — the rubric grades mechanisms, measurements and
211	the soak — and fab turnaround lands on top of critical path B, already the likeliest cause
212	of an M2 slip. A breadboard plus an off-the-shelf MCP2515 module clears every guardrail, and
213	the handout is explicit that a food container is an acceptable enclosure.
214	
215	**Why the schematic is still worth the hours.** Three graded artifacts depend on it:
216	`docs/DESIGN.md` needs a defensible wiring story; `docs/hardware/wiring.md` needs pin assignments
217	that cannot drift from the build; and the three-isolated-workers test needs a parts-only
218	buyer who can order from the BOM without seeing the design. A hand-maintained pin table will
219	disagree with reality by Week 9. A generated one cannot.
220	
221	**Consequences.** `make hwcheck` (ERC) and `make hwdocs` (SVG, BOM, netlist) enter the
222	build. `docs/hardware/wiring.md` and `BOM.md` become **derived** artifacts. `CLAUDE.md`
223	§7.12 requires a rendered schematic in any PR touching hardware.
224	
225	### A.5 — ERC is a build failure, and the schematic SVG is committed 🔒
226	
227	`D-010` · Decided M0 · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
228	
229	*Note 2026-10-27, not a reopening: nothing has been drawn yet, so `docs/figures/` and its
230	SVG do not exist; the first PR that draws a block commits them (`hwgate`).*
231	
232	**Decision.** `kicad-cli sch erc --exit-code-violations` runs as `make hwcheck`; violations
233	fail the build. `make hwdocs` renders the schematic to `docs/figures/electricalDrawing.svg`,
234	and that SVG is **committed**.
235	
236	**Why the ERC gate.** It makes electrical correctness the same kind of object as
237	`-Wall -Wextra -Werror`: a machine-checked precondition rather than a thing someone
238	remembers to look at. Unconnected pins and power-output conflicts are exactly the class of
239	error that survives a human read and kills a board.
240	
241	**Why commit a generated file.** Normally we would not. But a reviewer cannot read a diff
242	of S-expression coordinates, and §7.6 says a PR nobody understands does not merge — so
243	without a rendered picture, hardware would fall outside the review process entirely. The
244	SVG is the diff a human can actually read. It is regenerated, never hand-edited.
245	
246	**Open sub-item (Lance, M2):** `sym-lib-table` referenced `CS370_Project_Library.kicad_sym`,
247	which did not exist — KiCad errors on project open. An empty library is committed to resolve
248	it; populate it as parts are drawn.
249	
250	### A.6 — One box, one USB-C input, and a seconds-scale supercapacitor ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
251	
252	`D-024` · Decided M2, 2026-10-21 · **By:** Camden (in session) + Claude
253	· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
254	· **Supersedes:** D-011 (§G.9) · **Revises:** D-019's "the Pi, powered from the car's USB"
255	
256	**Decision.** The product is one small box, plus the Bluetooth OBD2 dongle (D-019) in the
257	car's OBD2 port.
258	
259	- **One port.** A single USB-C receptacle is the box's only power input. The owner plugs
260	  it into whatever USB-C charger and cable they already have in the car. The box is a
261	  plain sink (5.1 kΩ on both CC pins), so no source offers it more than 5 V.
262	- **One light, no buttons, no other ports** (light: D-027). Nothing on the car is cut,
263	  spliced, pierced or clamped.
264	- **Off at rest.** The box runs only while its source is live. At key-off the source
265	  disappears; the box sees it on a source-present GPIO, waits out a short grace period,
266	  commits and checkpoints its storage, and halts. The power stage then cuts the Pi's
267	  supply, and the box stays dark until the next start, when it boots by itself.
268	- **A small supercapacitor bank** covers brief shortfalls, rides through the dip at
269	  engine start where it can, and powers the clean shutdown. A seconds-scale bank cannot
270	  make up for a source that is too weak for a whole drive; see the limits below. It is
271	  short-lived by design: the goal is seconds to tens of seconds of runtime, about one
272	  minute is the ceiling, and it is never an always-on supply.
273	- **Clean shutdown is the normal path; crash consistency is the guarantee.** If the bank
274	  is empty, the cable is pulled or the Pi resets at crank, storage recovers at the next
275	  boot (mechanism D).
276	
277	**The power block's requirements.** Parts come only from datasheets a human has checked
278	(`CLAUDE.md` §8.4), and nothing is ordered until the design is signed.
279	
280	1. Sink only, 5 V only; transient and reverse-polarity protection; a fuse.
281	2. An input current limit below what the source advertises, and an inrush limiter,
282	   because an empty bank looks like a short circuit. A plain sink does not know the
283	   source's rating, so the box reads the source's CC advertisement (USB default, 1.5 A or
284	   3 A). The Pi has no analog inputs, so that takes a detector part (comparators or a
285	   USB-C controller IC) that reports the level on GPIOs.
286	3. Power path: the source feeds the Pi first; the bank covers only the shortfall or the
287	   gap.
288	4. A source-present signal on a GPIO, divided down to 3.3 V.
289	5. A halt-done signal: once the Pi has halted, the power stage removes the Pi's supply
290	   **even if the source has come back**, holds it off briefly, then re-enables. Otherwise
291	   a source that returns mid-shutdown leaves a halted Pi and a dark box in a running car.
292	6. Auto power-on when the source returns, with no button.
293	7. A 5 V, 3 A converter to the Pi that can step up, because the bank's voltage falls as it
294	   discharges.
295	
296	**Estimates, not measurements.** Each is replaced by a measured value before it appears
297	in `docs/DESIGN.md` as anything but an estimate (`powerspec`, `capbench`).
298	
299	| Quantity | Estimate |
300	| --- | --- |
301	| Pi 4 draw during boot and shutdown | 3 to 5 W |
302	| Grace period before shutdown starts (longer than a crank dip) | about 3 s × 4 W ÷ 0.85 ≈ 15 J |
303	| Clean-shutdown energy | 10–15 s × 4 W ÷ 0.85 converter efficiency ≈ 50–70 J |
304	| Crank-bridge energy | 1–3 s × 5 W ≈ 5–15 J |
305	| Two 2.7 V cells in series, 10 F total, charged to about 5 V | ½·C·V² ≈ 125 J stored; about 105 J usable above a 2 V converter floor, about 20 s at 4 W |
306	| Charge time from empty at a 1 A budget | 10 F × 5 V ÷ 1 A ≈ 50 s; slower on a 1.5 A source that is also running the Pi |
307	
308	The margin is thin: grace plus shutdown come to about 65–85 J against about 105 J usable,
309	before the radios' draw is counted. `powerspec` replaces every row with a measurement and
310	states the margin.
311	
312	**Limits, stated plainly.**
313	
314	- **Cold start.** The bank is empty at the first key-on of a session, so it cannot bridge
315	  that crank dip, and the Pi may reset while cranking. That is survivable only because
316	  storage is crash-consistent. Crank bridging is best-effort; the key-off shutdown is the
317	  reliable path.
318	- **Always-live sources are not supported.** On a charger that stays live with the key
319	  off, the box stays on, and the Pi plus the dongle can drain the car's battery over a few
320	  days. This is an installation requirement, not a mode we engineer around, but whether
321	  the box should halt itself after a long stretch with the engine silent is open
322	  (`shutfsm`).
323	- **Weak sources.** A charger that advertises only default USB current (500 or 900 mA)
324	  cannot run a Pi 4 with both radios, and the bank cannot make up the difference for a
325	  whole drive. What the box does then (refuse to start and show red, or run degraded) is
326	  open (`powerspec`).
327	- **Boot time.** A stock Pi 4 boots in roughly half a minute (estimate, `bootbudget`), so
328	  the start of each drive's warm-up goes unrecorded.
329	- **Demo day.** The box is off unless powered, and the handout's live demonstration runs
330	  on live sensors (§5, §11), so the demo needs a running testbed car on site, or an
331	  arrangement with the professor (`democar`).
332	- **The dongle still draws from OBD2 pin 16 with the key off** (D-019). Its key-off
333	  current is measured before it stays plugged in overnight (`dongledrain`).
334	
335	**Why one box.** Camden's design, 2026-10-21 (`docs/REVISION_PLAN.md` §1.1, P7–P10,
336	P13): "no need to reinvent the charger." The owner already has a USB-C charger, so the
337	team designs the box and buys only the dongle and a cable. One port and one light is a
338	product an ordinary owner can install.
339	
340	**Why a supercapacitor.** Camden's choice, 2026-10-21 (R1). A lithium cell must not
341	charge above about 45 °C or below 0 °C, and a car cabin leaves that window at both ends;
342	many cheap Pi UPS boards have no temperature cutoff. A supercapacitor has no
343	thermal-runaway failure, tolerates a wider temperature range (confirm against the part's
344	datasheet), and fits a seconds-scale job. Its costs are low voltage per cell (two in
345	series, with balancing), very low internal resistance (so a fuse), and fast
346	self-discharge, which does not matter for a box that is off at rest.
347	
348	**Alternatives rejected.** The car's USB wired straight to the Pi (D-011): no warning
349	before power loss, so every key-off cut a write. A small lithium cell: the charge
350	temperature window above. A wake button: dropped (P10).
351	
352	**Cost.** A power block to design, draw, buy and bench-test, on the hardware critical
353	path (`powerspec`, `schpower`, `capbench`), and more to measure before any claim
354	(`keyoff`, `cranklog`, `expshut`).
355	
356	### A.7 — Standard Mode 01 requests are the primary data path ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
357	
358	`D-012` · Decided M1, 2026-09-21 · **By:** Camden + Claude
359	· **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
360	
361	*Revised 2026-09-21 by D-015, before any review: the CAN-level detail (arbitration IDs,
362	broadcast frames, a listen-only flag, the port-traffic check) went with the MCP2515.*
363	
364	**Decision.** The capture daemon gets its signals by sending **standard OBD2 Mode 01
365	requests** through the OBD2 adapter (D-019) on a fixed, rate-limited, round-robin schedule,
366	one request outstanding at a time. Every timeout and every unanswered PID is logged.
367	
368	**Why.** D-011 (now D-024) makes this a plug-in device, and the thing that makes a plug-in
369	device work on a car it has never seen is the part of the protocol every car must speak:
370	Mode 01 is mandatory on US cars from model year 1996. *"Learns this car's normal"* is
371	precisely what lets one device serve different cars without per-model decode work: it
372	never needs to know what normal *is* ahead of time.
373	
374	**Sample-rate consequence.** Signals are round-robined, so each PID is sampled at
375	(request rate ÷ PID count) — on the order of 1 Hz each for a ~10 requests/s budget over
376	~8 PIDs. That is ample for what we watch (warm-up over minutes, fuel trim against load,
377	drift over days) and must be stated in `docs/DESIGN.md` §1. The request budget itself
378	is a design-doc number to justify, not a constant to pick.
379	
380	**Cost.** The device sends requests to the car's ECU. Kept safe by the rate limit, one
381	outstanding request, and only standard read-only Mode 01 requests — the same thing every
382	scan tool does.
383	
384	**Scope note.** "Works on any car" is the product's direction, not our claim. The claim is
385	E.1 (D-021): one car, a learned normal, fault areas named, measured error rates.
386	
387	### A.8 — A real-time clock keeps wall time while the box is off ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
388	
389	`D-030` · Decided M2, 2026-10-21 · **By:** Camden (in session) + Claude
390	· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
391	
392	**Decision.** The box gets a small real-time clock module on the Pi's I2C bus, kept
393	running by its own backup cell or capacitor while the box is off. At boot the system
394	clock is set from it. If the clock reports its time as invalid (its backup was lost),
395	that session's wall time is marked untrusted. Every record still carries `mono_ns`
396	regardless. The phone page stays read-only: it does not set the clock.
397	
398	**Why.** The Pi has no battery-backed clock, and the box has no network (`CLAUDE.md`
399	§2.3). Raspberry Pi OS's `fake-hwclock` restores the time saved at the last shutdown, so
400	the clock does not advance while the box is off, and every boot would appear to follow the
401	previous shutdown directly. The soak (D-023) must prove a 48-hour wall-clock span across
402	parked gaps, and the report's session list needs real times. Camden chose the clock
403	module, 2026-10-21, over the phone setting the time (that depends on someone opening the
404	page on every drive) and over no wall clock at all (`docs/REVISION_PLAN.md` §1.2, R5).
405	
406	**Cost.**
407	
408	- One more part, on I2C (GPIO2 and GPIO3, header pins 3 and 5), drawn in the Pi interface
409	  block, and bought only after the design is signed.
410	- Its backup cell or capacitor lives in a parked car's cabin, so its temperature rating
411	  must cover that, checked against the part's datasheet (`rtcspec`).
412	- A clock that has drifted or lost its backup must be detected rather than trusted, so the
413	  boot path checks it (`rtcboot`).
414	
415	---
416	
417	## B. Systems architecture and mechanisms
418	
419	### B.1 — Mechanism commitments: D and E; B and F declined ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
420	
421	`D-017` · Decided M1, 2026-09-21 · **By:** Camden + Claude
422	· **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
423	· **Supersedes:** D-002 (§G.3)
424	
425	*B and F declined 2026-10-21 by D-029 (§B.7), before any review: no Pi-side sensor will be
426	added, so D and E are the committed pair and the "only if" rows below no longer apply.*
427	
428	The handout requires two, implemented by us and measured.
429	
430	| Mechanism | Status | Where |
431	| --- | --- | --- |
432	| **D** — custom append-only storage, crash-consistent | **committed** | `src/store/` |
433	| **E** — multi-process with a supervisor | **committed** | `src/supervisor/`, `src/ipc/` |
434	| **B** — interrupt-driven input with a polling comparison | declined (D-029) | — |
435	| **F** — high-rate no-drop SPSC ring | declined (D-029) | — |
436	| **A**, **C**, raw CAN | stretch, after D and E are measured | — |
437	
438	**D.** *Power disappears every time the key turns off* (D-024). The box shuts down
439	cleanly on its supercapacitor when it can, but the bank is empty at a cold start, a
440	pulled cable beats it, and a crank dip can reset the Pi, so storage must survive a cut at
441	any instant. *(Revised 2026-10-21 by D-024; it read "we never get a clean shutdown".)*
442	Measured by cutting the Pi's own 5 V rail mid-write, after the converter so the
443	supercapacitor cannot cover it, repeatedly, and proving recovery (`expcrash`). Pulling
444	the charger no longer tests this: it triggers a clean shutdown.
445	
446	**E.** A recorder that dies silently has actively harmed its user, who believes it is on
447	duty. Any child may be `kill -9`'d; the system degrades, logs, recovers. Measured by killing
448	each child repeatedly and timing detection and recovery (`expkill`).
449	
450	**Why B and F left the OBD data path (D-015, D-019).** B needs an interrupt that *our*
451	design services. The adapter's interrupts belong to the kernel's Bluetooth and RFCOMM
452	stack; our process only blocks on a tty, and at ~10–20 replies/s a poll loop keeps up
453	trivially — the comparison would measure the tty layer, not a design of ours. F needs a
454	*high-rate* stream; ~10–20 samples/s never stresses a ring, so "zero drops under
455	contention" would be true and meaningless.
456	
457	**What brings them back.** An MPU-6050 on the Pi's I2C, its `INT` pin on a GPIO: kHz
458	samples from a hardware FIFO give a real interrupt-vs-polling comparison (B) and a rate
459	that stresses the ring (F). That was board item `pisensor`; D-029 declined it.
460	
461	**The ring stays regardless.** It is how capture hands samples to storage across the
462	process boundary E requires, and B.3 still binds it.
463	
464	**Risk.** D and E alone meet the floor exactly. If either measurement fails, nothing is in
465	reserve. `pisensor` was that reserve, and D-029 declined it.
466	
467	### B.2 — Four processes, not one 🔒
468	
469	`D-002` (corollary) · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
470	
471	`obdd`, `storaged`, `analyzed` and `supervisor` are separate processes with separate
472	address spaces, communicating over a shared-memory ring and Unix domain sockets.
473	
474	**Why.** Fault isolation is the product requirement, not an architectural preference: the
475	analysis engine is the most complex and least trustworthy component, and it must not be
476	able to take the capture path down with it. One process would be simpler and would fail
477	the thing the device exists to do.
478	
479	### B.3 — The ring refuses rather than overwrites 🔒
480	
481	Decided M0 · **By:** Claude, from D-002 · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
482	
483	When the ring is full the producer returns failure and increments an overrun counter. It
484	does **not** overwrite the oldest unread slot.
485	
486	**Why.** Overwriting loses data silently, and silent loss is the exact failure mechanism F
487	exists to make impossible. A refusal is visible, countable, and reportable; an overwrite
488	looks like a quiet minute. Enforced by `tests/test_ring.c`.
489	
490	**Reviewer note.** This is a real trade: under sustained overload we drop *new* data
491	rather than *old*. If that is ever the wrong choice for a diagnostic, reopen this.
492	
493	### B.4 — The phone is a read-only window over the device's own Wi-Fi ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
494	
495	`D-013` · Decided M1, 2026-09-21 · **By:** Camden + Claude
496	· **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
497	
498	*Extended 2026-10-21 by D-028 (§B.6): the page also shows trends and downloads a report,
499	and the server-language sub-decision below is closed (C).*
500

# Decision log — carwatch

**Purpose:** every design decision on this project, in one place, organized by category so
you can find what you need without knowing an ID. This is an **audit log**, not a
reference doc — its job is to let Camden and Lance verify, after any working session,
that no decision was made on their behalf that they disagree with.

**This file holds what is DECIDED. Open work and open questions live on the board**,
`docs/milestones.md`, mirrored to GitHub issues, with no pre-assigned owners (D-020, D-026,
`CLAUDE.md` §7.11).
An ❓ OPEN entry below exists only as a pointer to its issue, so the reasoning sits beside
the decisions it will eventually join.

## How to use this file

**After every Claude Code session, read the Review Queue below.** It lists every
decision that no human has signed off on yet. That is the whole point of this file.

**After your partner's session, skim the Review Queue too.** Their agent's choices bind
your subsystems as surely as yours do.

## Status legend

| Mark | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 🔒 **LOCKED** | Decided and human-approved. Not reopened without saying so explicitly and getting a yes. |
| ⚠️ **UNREVIEWED** | Made by Claude during a session without a human in the loop. **Binding on nothing until a human signs it.** |
| ❓ **OPEN** | Not decided. Blocking something. Tracked by a board item. |
| 🗑 **SUPERSEDED** | Replaced. Kept with a pointer, never deleted — the reasoning is evidence. |

**Claude may never change a decision's status to LOCKED.** Only Camden or Lance does
that, by editing the `Reviewed` field, in a commit authored by that human.

---

## ⚠️ REVIEW QUEUE — read this first

Decisions currently awaiting a human signature:

| ID | Decision | Made by | Session date | Reviewer needed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D-007 | Honda testbed is a 2015 Honda CR-V EX-L (§A.3) | Camden + Claude | 2026-09-21 | Lance — it is your car; confirm the engine and transmission from the VIN and sign |
| D-008 | Milestone dates verified against the syllabus (§F.3) | Camden | 2026-09-21 | Camden — your answer; mark it LOCKED in your own commit |

## A. Hardware and interfaces

### A.1 — The Pi reads OBD2 over a Bluetooth Classic adapter; USB is the fallback ⚠️ UNREVIEWED

`D-019` · Decided M1, 2026-09-23 · **By:** Camden (in session) + Claude
· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
· **Supersedes:** D-015 (§G.4)

*Pi power revised 2026-10-21 by D-024 (§A.6), before any review: the Pi is in a box fed
by the owner's USB-C charger, not wired to the car's USB. The adapter's key-off draw is
now board item `dongledrain`.*

**Decision.** An **OBDLink LX** (STN chip, **Bluetooth Classic, Serial Port Profile**; not
BLE) plugs into the OBD2 port. The Pi, in the box (D-024), talks to it with
its built-in Bluetooth radio over RFCOMM. Provisioning pairs and trusts the adapter once,
binds it with `rfcomm bind` to `/dev/rfcomm0`, and a udev rule links that to **`/dev/obd`**,
so every consumer still opens `/dev/obd` and sends Mode 01 requests (D-012). No MCP2515, no
SPI, no CAN wiring, and no data cable in the cabin.

**Raw CAN is still a stretch goal**: an MCP2515 on SPI, taken up only after mechanisms D
and E are implemented *and measured* (unchanged from D-015).

**Why.** Camden's call, 2026-09-23: the goal is the simplest data path that works. The box
becomes one power cable; the adapter stays in the port. The protocol, the parsing and every
downstream design are the same as D-015, because an STN adapter speaks the same ELM327
command set over Bluetooth as over USB.

*Note 2026-10-27: D-038 rewrote `make boundary`. `AF_BLUETOOTH` is now banned everywhere,
and Unix sockets are allowed through `src/ipc/uds.c`, so the reasoning below still holds.*

**Why a tty and not our own Bluetooth socket.** Opening an RFCOMM socket from `obdd` would
put `socket()` in `src/obd/`, which `make boundary` forbids outside `src/interface/`
(CLAUDE.md §2.1). Letting the kernel's RFCOMM layer present a tty keeps the boundary check
meaningful and keeps `obdd` a plain serial reader.

**What D-001 (§G.1) said against this, and why it no longer applies.** G.1 rejected a
Bluetooth ELM327 because it gives up interrupts and bus-level timing, taking mechanisms A,
B, C and F with it. D-015 already accepted exactly that loss for the USB adapter, and D-017
records what survives (D and E). Bluetooth costs no further mechanism.

**Costs and risks.**

- **Provisioning.** Pairing, trust and a persistent bind must survive reboots and every
  key-off (`scripts/provision_pi.sh`, board item `bench`).
- **A new failure mode.** The link can drop while the engine runs (adapter out of range,
  adapter asleep, radio interference). `obdd` sees a hangup on the tty and must reconnect
  with backoff, not crash-loop (`docs/DESIGN.md` §4, `supbackoff`).
- **One radio, two jobs.** The Pi 4's single Wi-Fi/Bluetooth chip also runs the phone
  access point (D-013). Coexistence is expected to work but is unmeasured: board item
  `btcoex`. Putting the access point on 5 GHz is the first mitigation to try.
- **Key-off draw.** The adapter still draws from OBD2 pin 16, live with the key off, and a
  Bluetooth adapter keeps a radio up. Its sleep behavior and key-off current are measured
  before it stays plugged in overnight (`dongledrain`).

**Fallback.** The USB adapter of D-015 (§G.4) needs only a different udev rule to appear as
`/dev/obd`. If Bluetooth proves unreliable in the car, switching back is a provisioning
change, not a code change.

### A.5 — ERC is a build failure, and the schematic SVG is committed 🔒

`D-010` · Decided M0 · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜

*Note 2026-10-27, not a reopening: nothing has been drawn yet, so `docs/figures/` and its
SVG do not exist; the first PR that draws a block commits them (`hwgate`).*

**Decision.** `kicad-cli sch erc --exit-code-violations` runs as `make hwcheck`; violations
fail the build. `make hwdocs` renders the schematic to `docs/figures/electricalDrawing.svg`,
and that SVG is **committed**.

**Why the ERC gate.** It makes electrical correctness the same kind of object as
`-Wall -Wextra -Werror`: a machine-checked precondition rather than a thing someone
remembers to look at. Unconnected pins and power-output conflicts are exactly the class of
error that survives a human read and kills a board.

**Why commit a generated file.** Normally we would not. But a reviewer cannot read a diff
of S-expression coordinates, and §7.6 says a PR nobody understands does not merge — so
without a rendered picture, hardware would fall outside the review process entirely. The
SVG is the diff a human can actually read. It is regenerated, never hand-edited.

**Open sub-item (Lance, M2):** `sym-lib-table` referenced `CS370_Project_Library.kicad_sym`,
which did not exist — KiCad errors on project open. An empty library is committed to resolve

### A.6 — One box, one USB-C input, and a seconds-scale supercapacitor ⚠️ UNREVIEWED

`D-024` · Decided M2, 2026-10-21 · **By:** Camden (in session) + Claude
· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
· **Supersedes:** D-011 (§G.9) · **Revises:** D-019's "the Pi, powered from the car's USB"

**Decision.** The product is one small box, plus the Bluetooth OBD2 dongle (D-019) in the
car's OBD2 port.

- **One port.** A single USB-C receptacle is the box's only power input. The owner plugs
  it into whatever USB-C charger and cable they already have in the car. The box is a
  plain sink (5.1 kΩ on both CC pins), so no source offers it more than 5 V.
- **One light, no buttons, no other ports** (light: D-027). Nothing on the car is cut,
  spliced, pierced or clamped.
- **Off at rest.** The box runs only while its source is live. At key-off the source
  disappears; the box sees it on a source-present GPIO, waits out a short grace period,
  commits and checkpoints its storage, and halts. The power stage then cuts the Pi's
  supply, and the box stays dark until the next start, when it boots by itself.
- **A small supercapacitor bank** covers brief shortfalls, rides through the dip at
  engine start where it can, and powers the clean shutdown. A seconds-scale bank cannot
  make up for a source that is too weak for a whole drive; see the limits below. It is
  short-lived by design: the goal is seconds to tens of seconds of runtime, about one
  minute is the ceiling, and it is never an always-on supply.
- **Clean shutdown is the normal path; crash consistency is the guarantee.** If the bank
  is empty, the cable is pulled or the Pi resets at crank, storage recovers at the next
  boot (mechanism D).

**The power block's requirements.** Parts come only from datasheets a human has checked
(`CLAUDE.md` §8.4), and nothing is ordered until the design is signed.

1. Sink only, 5 V only; transient and reverse-polarity protection; a fuse.
2. An input current limit below what the source advertises, and an inrush limiter,
   because an empty bank looks like a short circuit. A plain sink does not know the
   source's rating, so the box reads the source's CC advertisement (USB default, 1.5 A or
   3 A). The Pi has no analog inputs, so that takes a detector part (comparators or a
   USB-C controller IC) that reports the level on GPIOs.
3. Power path: the source feeds the Pi first; the bank covers only the shortfall or the
   gap.
4. A source-present signal on a GPIO, divided down to 3.3 V.
5. A halt-done signal: once the Pi has halted, the power stage removes the Pi's supply
   **even if the source has come back**, holds it off briefly, then re-enables. Otherwise
   a source that returns mid-shutdown leaves a halted Pi and a dark box in a running car.
6. Auto power-on when the source returns, with no button.
7. A 5 V, 3 A converter to the Pi that can step up, because the bank's voltage falls as it
   discharges.

**Estimates, not measurements.** Each is replaced by a measured value before it appears
in `docs/DESIGN.md` as anything but an estimate (`powerspec`, `capbench`).

| Quantity | Estimate |
| --- | --- |
| Pi 4 draw during boot and shutdown | 3 to 5 W |
| Grace period before shutdown starts (longer than a crank dip) | about 3 s × 4 W ÷ 0.85 ≈ 15 J |
| Clean-shutdown energy | 10–15 s × 4 W ÷ 0.85 converter efficiency ≈ 50–70 J |
| Crank-bridge energy | 1–3 s × 5 W ≈ 5–15 J |
| Two 2.7 V cells in series, 10 F total, charged to about 5 V | ½·C·V² ≈ 125 J stored; about 105 J usable above a 2 V converter floor, about 20 s at 4 W |
| Charge time from empty at a 1 A budget | 10 F × 5 V ÷ 1 A ≈ 50 s; slower on a 1.5 A source that is also running the Pi |

The margin is thin: grace plus shutdown come to about 65–85 J against about 105 J usable,
before the radios' draw is counted. `powerspec` replaces every row with a measurement and
states the margin.

**Limits, stated plainly.**

- **Cold start.** The bank is empty at the first key-on of a session, so it cannot bridge
  that crank dip, and the Pi may reset while cranking. That is survivable only because
  storage is crash-consistent. Crank bridging is best-effort; the key-off shutdown is the
  reliable path.
- **Always-live sources are not supported.** On a charger that stays live with the key
  off, the box stays on, and the Pi plus the dongle can drain the car's battery over a few
  days. This is an installation requirement, not a mode we engineer around, but whether
  the box should halt itself after a long stretch with the engine silent is open
  (`shutfsm`).
- **Weak sources.** A charger that advertises only default USB current (500 or 900 mA)
  cannot run a Pi 4 with both radios, and the bank cannot make up the difference for a
  whole drive. What the box does then (refuse to start and show red, or run degraded) is
  open (`powerspec`).
- **Boot time.** A stock Pi 4 boots in roughly half a minute (estimate, `bootbudget`), so
  the start of each drive's warm-up goes unrecorded.
- **Demo day.** The box is off unless powered, and the handout's live demonstration runs
  on live sensors (§5, §11), so the demo needs a running testbed car on site, or an
  arrangement with the professor (`democar`).
- **The dongle still draws from OBD2 pin 16 with the key off** (D-019). Its key-off
  current is measured before it stays plugged in overnight (`dongledrain`).

**Why one box.** Camden's design, 2026-10-21 (`docs/REVISION_PLAN.md` §1.1, P7–P10,
P13): "no need to reinvent the charger." The owner already has a USB-C charger, so the
team designs the box and buys only the dongle and a cable. One port and one light is a
product an ordinary owner can install.

**Why a supercapacitor.** Camden's choice, 2026-10-21 (R1). A lithium cell must not
charge above about 45 °C or below 0 °C, and a car cabin leaves that window at both ends;
many cheap Pi UPS boards have no temperature cutoff. A supercapacitor has no
thermal-runaway failure, tolerates a wider temperature range (confirm against the part's
datasheet), and fits a seconds-scale job. Its costs are low voltage per cell (two in
series, with balancing), very low internal resistance (so a fuse), and fast
self-discharge, which does not matter for a box that is off at rest.

**Alternatives rejected.** The car's USB wired straight to the Pi (D-011): no warning
before power loss, so every key-off cut a write. A small lithium cell: the charge
temperature window above. A wake button: dropped (P10).

**Cost.** A power block to design, draw, buy and bench-test, on the hardware critical
path (`powerspec`, `schpower`, `capbench`), and more to measure before any claim
(`keyoff`, `cranklog`, `expshut`).

### A.7 — Standard Mode 01 requests are the primary data path ⚠️ UNREVIEWED

`D-012` · Decided M1, 2026-09-21 · **By:** Camden + Claude
· **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜

*Revised 2026-09-21 by D-015, before any review: the CAN-level detail (arbitration IDs,
broadcast frames, a listen-only flag, the port-traffic check) went with the MCP2515.*

**Decision.** The capture daemon gets its signals by sending **standard OBD2 Mode 01
requests** through the OBD2 adapter (D-019) on a fixed, rate-limited, round-robin schedule,
one request outstanding at a time. Every timeout and every unanswered PID is logged.

**Why.** D-011 (now D-024) makes this a plug-in device, and the thing that makes a plug-in
device work on a car it has never seen is the part of the protocol every car must speak:
Mode 01 is mandatory on US cars from model year 1996. *"Learns this car's normal"* is
precisely what lets one device serve different cars without per-model decode work: it
never needs to know what normal *is* ahead of time.

**Sample-rate consequence.** Signals are round-robined, so each PID is sampled at
(request rate ÷ PID count) — on the order of 1 Hz each for a ~10 requests/s budget over
~8 PIDs. That is ample for what we watch (warm-up over minutes, fuel trim against load,
drift over days) and must be stated in `docs/DESIGN.md` §1. The request budget itself
is a design-doc number to justify, not a constant to pick.

**Cost.** The device sends requests to the car's ECU. Kept safe by the rate limit, one
outstanding request, and only standard read-only Mode 01 requests — the same thing every
scan tool does.

**Scope note.** "Works on any car" is the product's direction, not our claim. The claim is
E.1 (D-021): one car, a learned normal, fault areas named, measured error rates.

### A.8 — A real-time clock keeps wall time while the box is off ⚠️ UNREVIEWED

`D-030` · Decided M2, 2026-10-21 · **By:** Camden (in session) + Claude
· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜

**Decision.** The box gets a small real-time clock module on the Pi's I2C bus, kept
running by its own backup cell or capacitor while the box is off. At boot the system
clock is set from it. If the clock reports its time as invalid (its backup was lost),
that session's wall time is marked untrusted. Every record still carries `mono_ns`
regardless. The phone page stays read-only: it does not set the clock.

**Why.** The Pi has no battery-backed clock, and the box has no network (`CLAUDE.md`
§2.3). Raspberry Pi OS's `fake-hwclock` restores the time saved at the last shutdown, so
the clock does not advance while the box is off, and every boot would appear to follow the
previous shutdown directly. The soak (D-023) must prove a 48-hour wall-clock span across
parked gaps, and the report's session list needs real times. Camden chose the clock
module, 2026-10-21, over the phone setting the time (that depends on someone opening the
page on every drive) and over no wall clock at all (`docs/REVISION_PLAN.md` §1.2, R5).

**Cost.**

- One more part, on I2C (GPIO2 and GPIO3, header pins 3 and 5), drawn in the Pi interface
  block, and bought only after the design is signed.
- Its backup cell or capacitor lives in a parked car's cabin, so its temperature rating
  must cover that, checked against the part's datasheet (`rtcspec`).
- A clock that has drifted or lost its backup must be detected rather than trusted, so the
  boot path checks it (`rtcboot`).

## B. Systems architecture and mechanisms

### B.1 — Mechanism commitments: D and E; B and F declined ⚠️ UNREVIEWED

`D-017` · Decided M1, 2026-09-21 · **By:** Camden + Claude
· **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
· **Supersedes:** D-002 (§G.3)

*B and F declined 2026-10-21 by D-029 (§B.7), before any review: no Pi-side sensor will be
added, so D and E are the committed pair and the "only if" rows below no longer apply.*

The handout requires two, implemented by us and measured.

| Mechanism | Status | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **D** — custom append-only storage, crash-consistent | **committed** | `src/store/` |
| **E** — multi-process with a supervisor | **committed** | `src/supervisor/`, `src/ipc/` |
| **B** — interrupt-driven input with a polling comparison | declined (D-029) | — |
| **F** — high-rate no-drop SPSC ring | declined (D-029) | — |
| **A**, **C**, raw CAN | stretch, after D and E are measured | — |

**D.** *Power disappears every time the key turns off* (D-024). The box shuts down
cleanly on its supercapacitor when it can, but the bank is empty at a cold start, a
pulled cable beats it, and a crank dip can reset the Pi, so storage must survive a cut at
any instant. *(Revised 2026-10-21 by D-024; it read "we never get a clean shutdown".)*
Measured by cutting the Pi's own 5 V rail mid-write, after the converter so the
supercapacitor cannot cover it, repeatedly, and proving recovery (`expcrash`). Pulling
the charger no longer tests this: it triggers a clean shutdown.

**E.** A recorder that dies silently has actively harmed its user, who believes it is on
duty. Any child may be `kill -9`'d; the system degrades, logs, recovers. Measured by killing
each child repeatedly and timing detection and recovery (`expkill`).

**Why B and F left the OBD data path (D-015, D-019).** B needs an interrupt that *our*
design services. The adapter's interrupts belong to the kernel's Bluetooth and RFCOMM
stack; our process only blocks on a tty, and at ~10–20 replies/s a poll loop keeps up
trivially — the comparison would measure the tty layer, not a design of ours. F needs a
*high-rate* stream; ~10–20 samples/s never stresses a ring, so "zero drops under
contention" would be true and meaningless.

**What brings them back.** An MPU-6050 on the Pi's I2C, its `INT` pin on a GPIO: kHz
samples from a hardware FIFO give a real interrupt-vs-polling comparison (B) and a rate
that stresses the ring (F). That was board item `pisensor`; D-029 declined it.

**The ring stays regardless.** It is how capture hands samples to storage across the
process boundary E requires, and B.3 still binds it.

**Risk.** D and E alone meet the floor exactly. If either measurement fails, nothing is in
reserve. `pisensor` was that reserve, and D-029 declined it.

### B.2 — Four processes, not one 🔒

`D-002` (corollary) · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜

`obdd`, `storaged`, `analyzed` and `supervisor` are separate processes with separate
address spaces, communicating over a shared-memory ring and Unix domain sockets.

**Why.** Fault isolation is the product requirement, not an architectural preference: the
analysis engine is the most complex and least trustworthy component, and it must not be
able to take the capture path down with it. One process would be simpler and would fail
the thing the device exists to do.

### B.3 — The ring refuses rather than overwrites 🔒

Decided M0 · **By:** Claude, from D-002 · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜

When the ring is full the producer returns failure and increments an overrun counter. It
does **not** overwrite the oldest unread slot.

**Why.** Overwriting loses data silently, and silent loss is the exact failure mechanism F
exists to make impossible. A refusal is visible, countable, and reportable; an overwrite
looks like a quiet minute. Enforced by `tests/test_ring.c`.

**Reviewer note.** This is a real trade: under sustained overload we drop *new* data
rather than *old*. If that is ever the wrong choice for a diagnostic, reopen this.

· **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜

*Extended 2026-10-21 by D-028 (§B.6): the page also shows trends and downloads a report,
and the server-language sub-decision below is closed (C).*

784	### B.10 — Events reach storage over one Unix socket to `storaged` (draft) ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
785	
786	`D-042` · Drafted M2, 2026-10-27 · **By:** Claude, in Camden's session
787	· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
788	· **Answers (if signed):** D-031's open item (§B.8) and board item `verdictpath`
789	
790	**Decision (draft).** Samples travel by the rings; everything else that must be durable
791	is an **event**, and events travel by one socket.
792	
793	- **The socket.** `storaged` listens on a Unix domain socket of type `SOCK_SEQPACKET`,
794	  `/run/carwatch/events.sock`, created by the supervisor's runtime directory, mode 0600.
795	  One packet is one event: `code` u16, then up to 200 bytes of `key=value` text. A
796	  sequenced packet socket keeps message boundaries and order and never splits an event.
797	- **Who sends.** Every daemon sends its own events: `analyzed` its verdicts (and also
798	  tells the supervisor, which drives the light), the supervisor its child, power and
799	  clock events, `obdd` and `ambientd` their link and sensor events. The event names are
800	  the failure table's log events (`docs/DESIGN.md` §4).
801	- **What `storaged` does.** It writes each event as an `event` record (D-034) in the next
802	  batch, so an event is durable at the same commit as the samples around it and is
803	  ordered with them by `seq`.
804	- **When `storaged` is down.** A sender keeps up to 64 unsent events in memory and drops
805	  the oldest beyond that, counting the drops; the count is in its heartbeat. Every event
806	  is also a log line in the journal at the moment it happens, so the journal is the
807	  record of last resort and the socket never blocks a sender (`MSG_DONTWAIT`).
808	
809	**Event codes.** High byte by sender, low byte by event: `0x01` supervisor, `0x02`
810	`obdd`, `0x03` `ambientd`, `0x04` `analyzed` (verdicts), `0x05` `storaged` itself (for
811	example `recovered`, `segment_dropped`). The table of codes lives in one header,
812	`include/common/events.h`, and nowhere else.
813	
814	**Why.** D-031 left this open, and the report (D-028) and `obdctl verdicts --since` need
815	verdicts and faults on disk, in order with the samples. One socket keeps `storaged` the
816	only writer of the log (C.1). A packet socket is the simplest IPC that keeps one event
817	one message. A sender that blocked on a dead `storaged` would let a storage fault stop
818	capture or analysis, which B.2 exists to prevent.
819	
820	**Cost.** One more listener in `storaged` and one more fd per sender. Events that arrive
821	while `storaged` is down and overflow the 64-event queue are lost from the log (but not
822	from the journal), and the drop count says how many. The socket is `AF_UNIX`, so the
823	boundary rule must allow it outside `src/interface/` (`make boundary`).
824	
825	**Alternative rejected.** Each process writing its own event file: several writers, no
826	common order with the samples, and one more crash-recovery story per file. Events in the
827	rings: the slot type is sized for a reply, and the supervisor, which has no ring, could
828	not send.

830	### B.11 — The supervisor's control socket, the five `obdctl` verbs, and `statusd` (draft) ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
831	
832	`D-043` · Drafted M2, 2026-10-27 · **By:** Claude, in Camden's session
833	· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
834	· **Answers (if signed):** board item `ipcspec`; names the status-page process D-013 and
835	D-028 left unnamed
836	
837	**Decision (draft).**
838	
839	- **The control socket.** The supervisor listens on `/run/carwatch/ctl.sock`, a Unix
840	  domain `SOCK_STREAM` socket, mode 0660. A request is one line, `VERB key=value ...`,
841	  at most 512 bytes. A reply is zero or more lines of `key=value` fields, then `ok`, or
842	  `err <code> <reason>`, then the connection closes. Text, so it can be typed by hand
843	  and quoted in the report and at the defense.
844	- **Routing.** The supervisor answers `status` itself, from its children's heartbeats.
845	  It forwards `verdicts`, `series` and `faults` to `storaged`, which reads its own
846	  committed log up to the durable offset (D-031), and `baseline` to `analyzed`, the only
847	  holder of baselines, each over that process's own query socket in the same format. A
848	  child that is down gives `err unavailable <name>`; nothing else waits on it.
849	
850	**The five verbs.**
851	
852	| Verb | Arguments | Answers |
853	| --- | --- | --- |
854	| `status` | none | each process: up, down or restarting, pid, uptime, restarts, RSS, CPU, event and drop counts; each ring's depth and overruns; dongle link and probe present or absent; the light's state; whether wall time is trusted; the mix of `src` in this session |
855	| `verdicts` | `--since WHEN` (default: this boot) | each surfaced verdict: start, end or active, fault area, the sensors that cooperated, residual, `src` |
856	| `series` | `PID --from WHEN --to WHEN [--binned]` | the samples of one PID (`0C`, or `probe`) in the window, each with `src`; `--binned` gives per-bin means instead |
857	| `baseline` | `PID [--bin RPM,LOAD,COOLANT]` | the learned mean and variance of one PID in every bin, or in the one bin named |
858	| `faults` | `--since WHEN` (default: this boot) | detection, degradation and recovery events (D-042), each with `src` |
859	
860	`WHEN` is ISO 8601 or relative (`-2h`). `obdctl` exits 0 on `ok`, 1 on `err`, 2 on a
861	usage error and 3 when the supervisor cannot be reached.
862	
863	**`statusd`.** The phone page and the report generator (D-013, D-028) are one supervised
864	process, `statusd`, in `src/interface/`. It serves HTTP only on the box's access-point
865	address, and builds every page and report from the same control-socket verbs, so it holds
866	no state of its own. It is the only process with an `AF_INET` socket.
867	
868	**Why.** Board item `ipcspec`: B.2, D-013 and D-031 all route queries through the
869	supervisor without saying how, the README's `baseline` line was ambiguous about bins,
870	and the status page had no process name for the failure table, the Makefile or the
871	soak's RSS plot. A line protocol over one socket is the smallest thing that lets the CLI,
872	the page and a human at a terminal ask the same questions. History is answered by
873	`storaged` because it owns the log; the supervisor does not hold data, so a query can
874	never slow the restart path.
875	
876	**Cost.** Three query sockets (supervisor, `storaged`, `analyzed`) and their parsers,
877	each a place for a malformed request to be handled; every parser gets a test with bad
878	input. History queries cost `storaged` reads while it writes, which the CPU measurement
879	(D-036) will show.
880	
881	**Alternative rejected.** `obdctl` reading the log files itself: simpler, but it breaks
882	D-031's rule that only the process holding the answer reads it, and the page would need a
883	second copy of that reader.

885	### B.12 — The rings live in shared memory the supervisor creates; `storaged` frees a slot only after `fsync` ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
886	
887	`D-039` · Decided M3, 2026-10-27 · **By:** Claude, in Camden's session
888	· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
889	· **Extends:** 🔒 B.3 (refuse, never overwrite), whose rule is unchanged; D-031 and
890	D-037 (one producer and one consumer per ring) · **Answers:** board item `ringshm`
891	
892	**Decision.**
893	
894	- **Peek, then release.** The consumer reads slots with `ring_peek` and frees them with
895	  `ring_release(n)`. `storaged` releases a batch's slots only after that batch's
896	  `COMMIT` has been `fsync`'d, so a `kill -9` of `storaged` before then loses nothing:
897	  the restarted `storaged` finds the same slots still in the ring.
898	- **The ring numbers its slots.** `ring_push` sets each slot's `seq` from the ring's own
899	  head, so numbering survives a producer restart and a gap is a real loss.
900	- **Lifecycle.** The supervisor creates each ring at start with `shm_open` and `mmap`
901	  (`ring_create`), removing a stale object left by a previous boot first. `obdd`,
902	  `ambientd` and `storaged` attach to it (`ring_attach`), which checks a header (magic,
903	  layout version, capacity, slot size) and refuses an object written by a different
904	  build. Only the creator initializes; a restarted child attaches and never resets the
905	  indices the other side is using.
906	- **Duplicates after a restart.** If `storaged` dies after `fsync` returns but before the
907	  release, the restarted process sees that batch again. So every batch also records, as
908	  an event, the `seq` of the newest ring slot it holds, and each run records which ring
909	  instance it drains (its generation, set at creation). After a restart, `storaged` skips
910	  slots at or below the last committed ring `seq`, but only for the same ring instance:
911	  a ring made fresh at the next boot is never skipped. A batch is never written twice.
912	
913	**Why.** With `ring_pop`, a slot left the ring the moment `storaged` read it, up to a
914	second before it was durable (D-035), so killing `storaged` (the soak's injected fault,
915	mechanism E's test) silently lost those samples, the loss B.3 exists to prevent. A
916	shared-memory ring that any child re-initializes on restart would reset the other side's
917	indices; a header check stops a ring left over from an older build being read with a new
918	layout.
919	
920	**Cost.** A ring holds at most 4096 slots, about 200 s at 20 samples a second, so a
921	`storaged` that is down longer makes the producer refuse (counted, B.3). Two small events
922	per batch (the ring generation once per run, the newest ring `seq` per batch). A first
923	draft skipped by `mono_ns` instead; the restart test lost a sample to two readings with
924	the same timestamp, which ring `seq` cannot have.
